# User stories

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 1, 6 · Agent: read-only

## Format

- Stories: `US-nnn`, "As a … I want … so that …", plus in-scope and out-of-scope notes.
- Acceptance criteria are given in `acceptance-criteria.md` as `AC-nnn-nn` (Given/When/Then), one observable behaviour each, each citing its `US` and any `BR`; the agent does not derive them.
- Do not invent behaviour a story does not state; record the gap as an `OQ` in `scope.md`.

## Stories

Epic: as a conference organizer, I want participants to register online, so that registrations are collected and managed reliably.

### US-001 External participant registration

As an external participant, I want to register using the external participant form, so that I can attend the conference and the activities I select.
In scope: the external form (BR-01), selecting active options (BR-04). Out of scope: payment, accounts, editing a submitted registration.

### US-002 Student registration

As a student, I want to register using the student form, so that I can attend the conference and the activities available to students.
In scope: the student form (BR-01), selecting active options (BR-04). Out of scope: verifying student status externally, accounts.

### US-003 Configurable conference options

As an organizer, I want workshops, events, meals and other optional activities to be configurable, so that the system can be reused when the programme changes.
Out of scope: an administration UI for options.

### US-004 Registration confirmation

As a participant, I want a clear confirmation in the application after my registration is processed, so that I know it was received (BR-06).

### US-005 Reliable registration storage

As an organizer, I want every accepted registration stored reliably, so that none is lost and each can be recovered (BR-07).

### US-006 Participant email confirmation

As a participant, I want an email confirming my registration, so that I have a record of it.

### US-007 Organizer notification

As an organizer, I want an email when someone registers, containing the submitted data with the raw registration JSON attached, so that I can monitor incoming registrations.

### US-008 Registration export

As an organizer, I want to export the current registrations as an Excel workbook, so that I can process them outside the system (BR-08).

### US-009 Organizer registration search

As an organizer, I want to search and filter the registrations in the application, so that I can find a participant or a group of participants without exporting every registration (BR-09, BR-10).
In scope: an organizer page and API that list registrations with a text search and filters by registration type and selected option, paged. Out of scope: editing or deleting registrations from the list, exporting the filtered list, saved searches.

# Definition of Done

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: phases 6, 7 · Agent: read-only

Applies to every project; project additions are `DoD-Pnn` in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md`.
Each item needs evidence in `docs/06_verification-report.md`.

| ID | Criterion | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| DoD-01 | The full test suite passes; frozen test hashes match the manifest | test report, hash check |
| DoD-02 | Format, lint, type check and static analysis report no errors | tool output |
| DoD-03 | The quality gate of `general/quality/measurement-scope.md` ("Quality gate") is met for each component, or the shortfall after the third survivor round is recorded with a decision | coverage and mutation reports with scope, raw and adjusted score, rounds |
| DoD-04 | Architecture constraints (`AR`) are checked automatically where possible; no dependency cycles | architecture test output |
| DoD-05 | No open Critical or High finding from the security review and scanners | `general/skills/verify-release` output |
| DoD-06 | Every component runs in its target environment and the core user flows work at runtime, not only in tests | runtime demonstration log |
| DoD-07 | Every AC traces to at least one test and one commit | traceability table |
| DoD-08 | Root and component READMEs (ES-06) work when followed from a clean checkout | clone log |
| DoD-09 | Release notes list everything a human must test manually | `docs/release-notes.md` |
| DoD-10 | Every decision has a resolution or is listed as pending review; inputs and protected files are unchanged | decisions log, `docs/00_input-manifest.sha256` check |
| DoD-11 | The evidence checks in `general/phases.md` hold | `general/phases.md`, "Evidence" |
# Measurement scope

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: phases 3, 5, 6 · Agent: read-only

Defines what test counts, coverage, mutation score and code size mean, so that figures from different runs compare. Record every figure in `run-log.json` → `codeMetrics` and in `docs/06_verification-report.md` with its scope, level and tool. The project selects paths and exclusions in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md` ("Mutation scope"); this file never names them.

## Constraints

- Do not change a tool's scope, filters, exclusions or thresholds to improve a number. A change is a decision record.
- Do not report a figure without its scope, level and tool.
- Production code is the source a component ships. It excludes tests, generated code, the application entry point and anything listed under "Measurement exclusions" in `docs/03_test-strategy.md` with a reason. Decide the exclusions in phase 3, before any test is written; do not extend them later.
- Test code never counts towards coverage or mutation.

## Test counts

Per component and level (`unit`, `integration`, `acceptance`, `architecture`, `e2e`), passed and failed, from the runner's own report.

## Coverage

Line and branch, per component, as three figures: `unit` (unit tests only), `nonUnit` (integration, acceptance and end-to-end tests that exercise the component) and `all` (one merged report). The headline figure is `all`.

## Mutation score

- **Scope:** all production code of the component, narrowed only to the paths in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md` "Mutation scope", which are the same in every run of the project (default: all production code). Do not narrow it by running only some tests or by excluding packages that are not listed there.
- **Tests:** the component's full automated suite, at every level it has, so the score does not depend on which level the agent ran. If that is infeasible, record the tests actually run and the reason in a decision record.
- **Record:** `{score, scoreAdjusted, scoreCovered, killed, equivalent, total, covered, scope, tests, tool, excluded}`. `score` (raw) = killed (timed-out counts as killed) ÷ all mutants the tool generated; a mutant no test reaches counts as survived. `scoreAdjusted` = (killed + equivalent) ÷ total, where `equivalent` is the number of survivors justified as equivalent. `scoreCovered` = killed ÷ mutants a test reaches.
- Do not remove equivalent mutants by hand. List every survivor you count as equivalent in `docs/03_test-strategy.md` with the class and method, the mutation and the reason it cannot change behaviour; a survivor without that entry is not equivalent. Always record the raw score next to the adjusted score.

## Code size

`cloc` (same version in every run): production = non-test source and resources, test = test sources including end-to-end tests. Generated code and lock files are excluded.

## Mutation run discipline

- Measure coverage and mutation score in phase 5, so that surviving mutants are handled before verification. Phase 6 repeats a measurement only for a component whose code or tests changed since, and only once, after the last fix.
- Do not start a full mutation run on code that is not final. One full run per component per measurement; the only other runs are the targeted survivor rounds and, only when the rule below requires it, one confirming full run.
- Check once, before the full run, that the tool works: a mutant in code the tests plainly cover must be killed. A score far below the line coverage (for example 25 % at 100 % coverage) means the tool is not activating mutants (known case: Stryker with the wrong Vitest major version); stop and raise a decision, do not record the figure.
- Start a long run in the background and continue with other checks of the phase; read its log only for the summary lines. Do not hold the session in a blocking wait on it.

## Quality gate

The gate is the same in every run of the project: the thresholds in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md` ("Thresholds"), per component, over the scope and with the tests defined above. It makes runs comparable: every run reaches the same quality, and what differs is the cost of reaching it.

- **Gate:** line coverage (`all`) at or above the line threshold, and `scoreAdjusted` at or above the mutation threshold. Branch coverage is recorded only.
- **Order in phase 5:** write the unit and integration tests area by area and measure line coverage after each area (fast) until the line threshold is met; then run mutation testing **once** per component (full run); then, if `scoreAdjusted` is below the threshold, up to **three** survivor rounds: each adds tests aimed at the survivors in the code that matters most (validation, security, persistence, business rules first) and re-runs only the mutated classes. After each round recompute `scoreAdjusted` for the component from the last full run plus the re-run classes (the classes that were not re-run keep their killed and total counts from the full run) and write the per-class numbers into `docs/03_test-strategy.md`. If the recomputed score is at least 1.0 point above the threshold the gate is met and no full run follows. # Metrics

> Owner: Experiment lead · Read in: every phase and post-run · Agent: read-only

Experiment measurement only. Record observed values; never estimate. An unobservable value stays `null` with a `<field>Reason`.

Goal column: **↓** lower is better, **↑** higher is better, **=** should equal the stated value, **i** information for interpreting other numbers.

## Principles

- **Human waiting is not part of the result.** Agent time is wall time minus every wait for a human. A wait over one hour also lets the 1-hour prompt cache expire, and the call after it writes the whole context again; that rebuild is a cost of the wait, so `usage.costUsdExclWaits` removes it. Compare runs on agent time and `costUsdExclWaits`.
- **Record only what only you can see, and with the clock tool.** The agent records what happened (waits, loops, decisions, deviations, test and quality results). Timestamps come from `tools/stat.mjs`, never from memory or estimates. Everything that can be computed from the transcripts and git is computed after the run by `tools/build-report.mjs`, so the run spends no calls on it.
- **Make runs comparable.** Say what a number covers. Scope, level and tool of coverage, mutation score and code size are defined in `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`.

## 1. Agent, during the run → `run-log.json`

Phase 0, first action: `node 03_statistics/tools/stat.mjs init`. It creates `run-log.json` from the template, a unique `runId`, the start time and commit, the transcript path and the environment. It prints what it wrote.

| Field | When | How | Goal |
|---|---|---|---|
| `runId`, `model`, `effort`, `templateVersion`, `start`, `startCommit`, `transcript`, `environment` | phase 0 | written by `stat.mjs init` from `run-config.md`, git and the host | i |
| `phases[].start`, `phases[].end` | every phase boundary | `stat.mjs phase <n> start` and `stat.mjs phase <n> end`; a start also closes the previous phase, `phase 7 end` also sets `end` and `finalCommit` | ↓ agent time per phase |
| `humanInterventions[]` | every time the agent waits for the human or the human acts, including stops, restarts and installs | `stat.mjs wait start <cause> "<reason>" [decisionId]` when you ask or stop, `stat.mjs wait end` when work resumes. `cause`: `decision`, `environment`, `approval`, `session`, `other` | ↓ count and minutes; every minute here is excluded from agent time |
| `firstTestRun`, `finalTestRun` | first full run before fixes; last full run | edit the file: `passed`, `failed` and `byLevel` (`unit`, `integration`, `acceptance`, `architecture`, `e2e` counts) | first: ↓ failed (defects the first run found); final: ↑ passed, `failed` = 0 |
| `acceptanceCriteria` | end of phase 3; changes in phase 4 | `total` criteria, `frozenTests`, `frozenTestChanges[]` as `{decisionId, reason}` | ↑ criteria covered by tests; ↓ frozen-test changes (each one needed a human) |
| `findings` | end of phase 6 | counts by severity, as found | ↓ |
| `openAtEnd` | end of phase 6 | Critical, High and Medium findings still open after triage | = 0 for Critical and High |
| `fixLoops[]` | each verify → fix → re-verify loop | `{loop, findings, category, needsHuman, change, start, end}`. `category`: `test-gap`, `security-config`, `dependency`, `defect`, `process`, `tooling`. `start` is the first fix action, `end` the clean re-check (UTC, `date -u +%FT%TZ`) | ↓ minutes per loop; a loop that repeats across runs belongs in the template |
| `decisions[]` | each decision record | `{id, type, phase, category, start, end}`; `type` `blocking` or `non-blocking`; `category`: `environment`, `dependency`, `security-finding`, `frozen-test`, `requirement`, `other`; `end` = when resolved | ↓ blocking; a category that repeats across runs can be answered in advance |
| `divergences[]` | whenever the run departs from `AGENTS.md`, `working-rules.md`, `phases.md` or the stack | `{phase, ref, divergence}`; includes steps done without the required question, scope reduced, versions replaced | = 0; each one makes the run less comparable |
| `codeMetrics` | phase 5, updated in phase 6 for a changed component | per component: `productionLoc`, `testLoc`, `lineCoverage` and `branchCoverage` as `{unit, nonUnit, all}`, `mutation` as `{score, scoreAdjusted, scoreCovered, killed, equivalent, total, covered, scope, tests, tool, excluded}`, plus complexity and duplication; scope, level and counting as in `general/quality/measurement-scope.md` | ↑ coverage and mutation score (always with scope); = 0 duplication |
| `codeMetrics.gate` | phase 5, updated in phase 6 | the quality gate of `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`: `thresholds`, `perComponent` (`lineMet`, `mutationMet`, shortfalls in points), `mutationRounds` and `testsAtFirstMutation` per component, `met` | `met` true; few rounds |

`commits[]` and `commitSummary` are not recorded by the agent: the post-run step reads them from `git log`.

## 2. Post-run session → `run-log.json`, `results/`, `data/`

Started automatically by the Stop and SessionEnd hooks in `.claude/settings.json` once `run-log.json` has an `end`; if the hooks did not run, in a new session whose only task is: "Run `node 03_statistics/tools/build-report.mjs --run 03_statistics` and report what it prints. Do not change anything else." Nothing is typed in by hand. The script:

1. measures the run from the session transcript(s), the sub-agent transcripts next to them and `git log`, and stores `time`, `usage`, `environment`, `commits`, `commitSummary` in `run-log.json`;
2. copies the transcripts to `03_statistics/data/` (committed with the run, so the measuring can be repeated on any machine; the recorded path is used when it exists, the copy otherwise);
3. writes everything it generates to `03_statistics/results/`: `run-report.html` (every attribute with goal, direction and value), `measurements.json`, `usage-summary.md`, `commits.csv`, `transcript.md` (readable session, needs Python 3);

Options: `--no-write` leaves `run-log.json` and `usage.md` alone, `--no-md` skips `transcript.md`, `--no-backup` skips `data/`. If `transcript` is missing from `run-log.json`, find the session with `py 03_statistics/tools/claude_chat_to_md.py --list`, put the path of its `.jsonl` in `transcript` (a resumed run lists every session file in `transcripts`) and run the script again. Without any transcript the report still builds from phases and recorded waits; cost, tokens, model and tool time, context and cache rebuilds are then not recorded.

| Field | What it is | Goal |
|---|---|---|
| `time.agentMin` | sum over phases of wall time minus waits (recorded interventions and idle gaps above 10 minutes in the transcript) | ↓ |
| `time.humanWaitMin`, `time.waitsOver60Min`, `time.longWaits[]` | excluded waiting, and each wait over an hour with its cause | ↓; = 0 waits over an hour |
| `time.modelMin`, `time.toolMin` | transcript time spent generating and running tools | ↓; tool time shows what to automate or speed up |
| `time.unrecordedIdleMin` | idle time in the transcript that `humanInterventions` does not cover | = 0 (a recording gap) |
| `time.phaseChecks` | phase boundaries written by `stat.mjs` against typed ones, and implausible timestamps | all via `stat.mjs`, no issues |
| `time.byPhase[]` | wall, wait, agent, model and tool minutes per phase | ↓ in phases 0, 1, 2, 7 (overhead); phases 4 to 6 hold the real work |
| `usage.inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `thinkingTokens`, `cacheReadTokens`, `cacheWriteTokens`, `modelCalls` | sums over every model call, each call counted once, sub-agents included | ↓ |
| `usage.toolCalls` | total, errors, per tool name | ↓ calls and errors |
| `usage.costUsd` | tokens × the prices in `usage.md`, per model | ↓ |
| `usage.costUsdExclWaits` | `costUsd` minus the cache rebuilds that followed a wait over an hour | ↓ (the comparison figure) |
| `usage.cacheRebuilds[]` | each cache write above 150k tokens, the wait before it and its extra cost | = none caused by waits |
| `usage.subagents` | sub-agent calls, transcripts found, their cost (inside `costUsd`) | i; a call without a transcript is a measuring gap |
| `usage.byPhase[]` | calls, tokens, cost and average context per phase | ↓ in late phases, where context is largest |
| `usage.context` | peak and average context tokens per call, share of calls above 150k | ↓ (every call re-reads the whole context) |
| `usage.toolTimeByCategory` | minutes and calls per command class (backend build, mutation, e2e, …) | ↓ for the largest classes |
| `commits[]` | per commit: phase, type, files, changed lines (without logs, lock files, generated folders), concerns touched, size and message checks, minutes since the previous commit (waits removed), model calls and cost since the previous commit | commits small and finished: ≤ 15 files and ≤ 400 lines, one concern, `<type>: <summary> (IDs)` |
| `commitSummary` | counts, median and maximum size, shares over the size guide, mixed, with a correct message, in a burst (within a minute of the previous), cost and minutes between commits, cost per 100 lines | ↓ oversize, mixed and burst; ↑ correct messages |
| `environment` | operator, machine, plan, permission mode (from `run-config.md`), the host the run started on (account, CPU, memory, working directory; read by `stat.mjs init`), operating system and tool versions (at the start), harness version, entry point, models, effort and permission modes seen (from the transcripts), measuring host | i; needed to explain differences between runs |

## 3. Human → `usage.md`

Prices before the post-run session (one row per model id, shape as in the file). After it only `Approval prompts` is yours; the other cells are filled automatically when empty, and anything you wrote stays. A mismatch between the harness's total and our calculation is reported in the last row.
# Run guide

> Feature experiment (template 1.7-ft): the folder name and branch follow `<user>/single-agent/sdd/v001/run-<n>[-<feature>]`, and greenfield and brownfield runs have extra steps. Clone with `--single-branch -b main` so the `experiment` branch never reaches the run folder.

This setup is run three times, once each by kyuhi, tanej and tjan, in one shared environment, and the three runs are compared. Everything below is therefore the same for everyone; the only things that may differ are the four lines in the table "If you are not kyuhi".

## 1. Prepare the run folder (clone, branch, .env)
1. **Clone the template** into a new folder named after the run (`kyuhi_single-agent_sdd_v007`). Branch `main` is the template you clone and never commit to it.

# Metrics

> Owner: Experiment lead · Read in: every phase and post-run · Agent: read-only

Experiment measurement only. Record observed values; never estimate. An unobservable value stays `null` with a `<field>Reason`.

Goal column: **↓** lower is better, **↑** higher is better, **=** should equal the stated value, **i** information for interpreting other numbers.

## Principles

- **Human waiting is not part of the result.** Agent time is wall time minus every wait for a human. A wait over one hour also lets the 1-hour prompt cache expire, and the call after it writes the whole context again; that rebuild is a cost of the wait, so `usage.costUsdExclWaits` removes it. Compare runs on agent time and `costUsdExclWaits`.
- **Record only what only you can see, and with the clock tool.** The agent records what happened (waits, loops, decisions, deviations, test and quality results). Timestamps come from `tools/stat.mjs`, never from memory or estimates. Everything that can be computed from the transcripts and git is computed after the run by `tools/build-report.mjs`, so the run spends no calls on it.
- **Make runs comparable.** Say what a number covers. Scope, level and tool of coverage, mutation score and code size are defined in `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`.

## 1. Agent, during the run → `run-log.json`

Phase 0, first action: `node 03_statistics/tools/stat.mjs init`. It creates `run-log.json` from the template, a unique `runId`, the start time and commit, the transcript path and the environment. It prints what it wrote.

| Field | When | How | Goal |
|---|---|---|---|
| `runId`, `model`, `effort`, `templateVersion`, `start`, `startCommit`, `transcript`, `environment` | phase 0 | written by `stat.mjs init` from `run-config.md`, git and the host | i |
| `phases[].start`, `phases[].end` | every phase boundary | `stat.mjs phase <n> start` and `stat.mjs phase <n> end`; a start also closes the previous phase, `phase 7 end` also sets `end` and `finalCommit` | ↓ agent time per phase |
| `humanInterventions[]` | every time the agent waits for the human or the human acts, including stops, restarts and installs | `stat.mjs wait start <cause> "<reason>" [decisionId]` when you ask or stop, `stat.mjs wait end` when work resumes. `cause`: `decision`, `environment`, `approval`, `session`, `other` | ↓ count and minutes; every minute here is excluded from agent time |
| `firstTestRun`, `finalTestRun` | first full run before fixes; last full run | edit the file: `passed`, `failed` and `byLevel` (`unit`, `integration`, `acceptance`, `architecture`, `e2e` counts) | first: ↓ failed (defects the first run found); final: ↑ passed, `failed` = 0 |
| `acceptanceCriteria` | end of phase 3; changes in phase 4 | `total` criteria, `frozenTests`, `frozenTestChanges[]` as `{decisionId, reason}` | ↑ criteria covered by tests; ↓ frozen-test changes (each one needed a human) |
| `findings` | end of phase 6 | counts by severity, as found | ↓ |
| `openAtEnd` | end of phase 6 | Critical, High and Medium findings still open after triage | = 0 for Critical and High |
| `fixLoops[]` | each verify → fix → re-verify loop | `{loop, findings, category, needsHuman, change, start, end}`. `category`: `test-gap`, `security-config`, `dependency`, `defect`, `process`, `tooling`. `start` is the first fix action, `end` the clean re-check (UTC, `date -u +%FT%TZ`) | ↓ minutes per loop; a loop that repeats across runs belongs in the template |
| `decisions[]` | each decision record | `{id, type, phase, category, start, end}`; `type` `blocking` or `non-blocking`; `category`: `environment`, `dependency`, `security-finding`, `frozen-test`, `requirement`, `other`; `end` = when resolved | ↓ blocking; a category that repeats across runs can be answered in advance |
| `divergences[]` | whenever the run departs from `AGENTS.md`, `working-rules.md`, `phases.md` or the stack | `{phase, ref, divergence}`; includes steps done without the required question, scope reduced, versions replaced | = 0; each one makes the run less comparable |
| `codeMetrics` | phase 5, updated in phase 6 for a changed component | per component: `productionLoc`, `testLoc`, `lineCoverage` and `branchCoverage` as `{unit, nonUnit, all}`, `mutation` as `{score, scoreAdjusted, scoreCovered, killed, equivalent, total, covered, scope, tests, tool, excluded}`, plus complexity and duplication; scope, level and counting as in `general/quality/measurement-scope.md` | ↑ coverage and mutation score (always with scope); = 0 duplication |
| `codeMetrics.gate` | phase 5, updated in phase 6 | the quality gate of `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`: `thresholds`, `perComponent` (`lineMet`, `mutationMet`, shortfalls in points), `mutationRounds` and `testsAtFirstMutation` per component, `met` | `met` true; few rounds |

`commits[]` and `commitSummary` are not recorded by the agent: the post-run step reads them from `git log`.

## 2. Post-run session → `run-log.json`, `results/`, `data/`

Started automatically by the Stop and SessionEnd hooks in `.claude/settings.json` once `run-log.json` has an `end`; if the hooks did not run, in a new session whose only task is: "Run `node 03_statistics/tools/build-report.mjs --run 03_statistics` and report what it prints. Do not change anything else." Nothing is typed in by hand. The script:

1. measures the run from the session transcript(s), the sub-agent transcripts next to them and `git log`, and stores `time`, `usage`, `environment`, `commits`, `commitSummary` in `run-log.json`;
2. copies the transcripts to `03_statistics/data/` (committed with the run, so the measuring can be repeated on any machine; the recorded path is used when it exists, the copy otherwise);
3. writes everything it generates to `03_statistics/results/`: `run-report.html` (every attribute with goal, direction and value), `measurements.json`, `usage-summary.md`, `commits.csv`, `transcript.md` (readable session, needs Python 3);

Options: `--no-write` leaves `run-log.json` and `usage.md` alone, `--no-md` skips `transcript.md`, `--no-backup` skips `data/`. If `transcript` is missing from `run-log.json`, find the session with `py 03_statistics/tools/claude_chat_to_md.py --list`, put the path of its `.jsonl` in `transcript` (a resumed run lists every session file in `transcripts`) and run the script again. Without any transcript the report still builds from phases and recorded waits; cost, tokens, model and tool time, context and cache rebuilds are then not recorded.

| Field | What it is | Goal |
|---|---|---|
| `time.agentMin` | sum over phases of wall time minus waits (recorded interventions and idle gaps above 10 minutes in the transcript) | ↓ |
| `time.humanWaitMin`, `time.waitsOver60Min`, `time.longWaits[]` | excluded waiting, and each wait over an hour with its cause | ↓; = 0 waits over an hour |
| `time.modelMin`, `time.toolMin` | transcript time spent generating and running tools | ↓; tool time shows what to automate or speed up |
| `time.unrecordedIdleMin` | idle time in the transcript that `humanInterventions` does not cover | = 0 (a recording gap) |
| `time.phaseChecks` | phase boundaries written by `stat.mjs` against typed ones, and implausible timestamps | all via `stat.mjs`, no issues |
| `time.byPhase[]` | wall, wait, agent, model and tool minutes per phase | ↓ in phases 0, 1, 2, 7 (overhead); phases 4 to 6 hold the real work |
| `usage.inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `thinkingTokens`, `cacheReadTokens`, `cacheWriteTokens`, `modelCalls` | sums over every model call, each call counted once, sub-agents included | ↓ |
| `usage.toolCalls` | total, errors, per tool name | ↓ calls and errors |
| `usage.costUsd` | tokens × the prices in `usage.md`, per model | ↓ |
| `usage.costUsdExclWaits` | `costUsd` minus the cache rebuilds that followed a wait over an hour | ↓ (the comparison figure) |
| `usage.cacheRebuilds[]` | each cache write above 150k tokens, the wait before it and its extra cost | = none caused by waits |
| `usage.subagents` | sub-agent calls, transcripts found, their cost (inside `costUsd`) | i; a call without a transcript is a measuring gap |
| `usage.byPhase[]` | calls, tokens, cost and average context per phase | ↓ in late phases, where context is largest |
| `usage.context` | peak and average context tokens per call, share of calls above 150k | ↓ (every call re-reads the whole context) |
| `usage.toolTimeByCategory` | minutes and calls per command class (backend build, mutation, e2e, …) | ↓ for the largest classes |
| `commits[]` | per commit: phase, type, files, changed lines (without logs, lock files, generated folders), concerns touched, size and message checks, minutes since the previous commit (waits removed), model calls and cost since the previous commit | commits small and finished: ≤ 15 files and ≤ 400 lines, one concern, `<type>: <summary> (IDs)` |
| `commitSummary` | counts, median and maximum size, shares over the size guide, mixed, with a correct message, in a burst (within a minute of the previous), cost and minutes between commits, cost per 100 lines | ↓ oversize, mixed and burst; ↑ correct messages |
| `environment` | operator, machine, plan, permission mode (from `run-config.md`), the host the run started on (account, CPU, memory, working directory; read by `stat.mjs init`), operating system and tool versions (at the start), harness version, entry point, models, effort and permission modes seen (from the transcripts), measuring host | i; needed to explain differences between runs |

## 3. Human → `usage.md`

Prices before the post-run session (one row per model id, shape as in the file). After it only `Approval prompts` is yours; the other cells are filled automatically when empty, and anything you wrote stays. A mismatch between the harness's total and our calculation is reported in the last row.

# Requirements check

> Written in: phase 1 · Source: `project/01_requirements/*` · Agent: writes

Story → criteria coverage and the gaps found in the inputs. Nothing is copied from the inputs; IDs refer to them.

## Story → criteria

| Story | Criteria (in `acceptance-criteria.md`) | Count | E2E scenario | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| US-001 | AC-001-01..08 | 8 | E2E-01 | ≥ 1 AC |
| US-002 | AC-002-01..07 | 7 | E2E-02 | ≥ 1 AC |
| US-003 | AC-003-01..03 | 3 | – (API-level only) | ≥ 1 AC |
| US-004 | AC-004-01..04 | 4 | E2E-01, E2E-02, E2E-03 | ≥ 1 AC |
| US-005 | AC-005-01..04 | 4 | E2E-01, E2E-04 | ≥ 1 AC |
| US-006 | AC-006-01..03 | 3 | E2E-01 | ≥ 1 AC |
| US-007 | AC-007-01..02 | 2 | E2E-01 | ≥ 1 AC |
| US-008 | AC-008-01..04 | 4 | E2E-04, E2E-05 | ≥ 1 AC |
| US-009 | AC-009-01..13 | 13 | E2E-06 | ≥ 1 AC |

Total 48 criteria, matching the stated total. Every criterion sits under exactly one story section and the traceability table maps it back, so every AC cites a story. Every rule BR-01..BR-10 is cited by at least one AC. Every e2e scenario cites only existing criteria and DoD-P items.

## Open questions

OQ-01..OQ-06 all have an answer in `scope.md`; they are product owner decisions and get no decision record.

## Requirements without their own criterion

SR-03 (rate and size limits), NFR-02 (persistence across container recreation) and NFR-04 (health and readiness) are covered in the specification and verified by runtime demonstration in phase 6, as the acceptance criteria file states. SR-02, SR-05..SR-09, SB-xx, AR-xx are mapped in phase 2.

## Gaps and contradictions

| # | Finding | Effect | Handling |
|---|---|---|---|
| G-1 | `scope.md` starts with a stray line before its title that repeats the answers of OQ-06..OQ-01 in reverse order. | Formatting only; the text matches the Open questions table. | Ignored; the table is authoritative. No decision needed. |
| G-2 | AC-006-03 cites `OQ-03` twice. | Typo, no behavioural effect. | None. |
| G-3 | `scope.md` priority 3 names US-007 and US-008 as organizer features but not US-009. | US-009 is an organizer feature too; ordering only. | Treated as an organizer feature (after the participant flow). No decision needed. |
| G-4 | AC-008-04 and AC-009-10 say the plain-HTTP organizer request is "refused" without a status code; `api-contract.md` fixes 401 only for missing or wrong credentials. | Two behaviours a client would notice (401 or 403). | D-10 (non-blocking, conservative default). |
| G-5 | AC-009-08 limits the search text to 100 characters, BR-10 says leading and trailing whitespace is ignored; whether the limit applies before or after trimming is not stated. | Visible only for a text over 100 characters that is at most 100 after trimming. | D-11 (non-blocking, conservative default). |
| G-6 | AC-009-08 rejects an option id that "is not a configured option"; an inactive option is still configured. | An inactive option id is a valid search filter (registrations may hold options deactivated later). | Follow the criterion literally: active and inactive configured ids are accepted, unknown ids are rejected. No decision needed. |

# Specification

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: `project/01_requirements/*`, `project/02_design/*`, `project/00_setup/tech-stack.md`, `project/00_setup/environments.md`, `general/security/*` · Agent: writes

Conference registration: a public registration form (external participants and students), storage in PostgreSQL plus a raw JSON copy, confirmation and organizer emails, an organizer Excel export and an organizer search page. The REST API is fixed by `api-contract.md` (AR-09) and described exactly by [`02_contracts/openapi.json`](02_contracts/openapi.json).

## 1. Components and runtime

| Component | Folder | Runs as | Talks to |
|---|---|---|---|
| backend | `02_output/backend` | Spring Boot jar in `eclipse-temurin` JRE image, non-root user, port 8080 | PostgreSQL (JDBC), SMTP, reCAPTCHA verify endpoint (HTTPS), JSON copy directory |
| frontend | `02_output/frontend` | React SPA built by Vite, served by `nginx` (non-root, port 8080), which also proxies `/api` to the backend | backend only through `/api` (AR-01) |
| postgres | image | `postgres` 16 with named volume `pgdata` | – |
| mailpit | image | local SMTP catcher (SMTP 1025, web/API 8025) | – |

Local stack: `02_output/docker-compose.yml`. Published on 127.0.0.1 only: backend `8080`, frontend `8081`, Mailpit `8025`. Named volumes `pgdata` and `jsoncopies` keep data across container recreation (NFR-02). Production: the same two images behind an external nginx that terminates TLS, serves `/` from the frontend and forwards `/api` to the backend with a fixed upstream `Host` (SR-08); a sample is in the backend README.

## 2. Backend architecture (AR-02, AR-03)

Ports-and-adapters with four layers under `si.konferenca.registration`:

| Package | Contents | May depend on |
|---|---|---|
| `domain` | registration model, types, option and consent definitions, conference configuration model, validation rules, search criteria, field errors | `java.*` only |
| `application` | use cases (`RegistrationService`, `SearchService`, `ExportService`) and the ports they need (`RegistrationStore`, `JsonCopyStore`, `CaptchaVerifier`, `Notifier`, `WorkbookWriter`) | `domain`, Spring stereotypes and transactions |
| `infrastructure.*` | adapters implementing the ports: `persistence` (JPA), `jsoncopy` (files), `mail` (SMTP), `captcha` (reCAPTCHA), `excel` (POI), `config` (options file loading, settings, startup checks) | `application`, `domain`, frameworks |
| `web` | REST controllers, request/response DTOs, error mapping, rate limit and body size filters | `application`, `domain` |
| `security` | Spring Security configuration, organizer authentication, HTTPS-only filter, headers, CORS | `domain`, `infrastructure.config` (settings), frameworks |

Justification: the business rules (validation, option availability, search semantics) are the code that must be mutation-tested most and change least; keeping them framework-free in `domain` makes them unit-testable and keeps the frameworks replaceable at the edges. `application` holds the one place where the storage order of BR-07/AR-05 is decided.

ArchUnit rules (written in phase 5, they check exactly this table):

1. `domain` depends only on `java..` classes.
2. `application` does not depend on `infrastructure..`, `web..` or `security..`.
3. `web` does not depend on `infrastructure..`.
4. `infrastructure..` does not depend on `web..` or `security..`.
5. No cycles between the slices `si.konferenca.registration.(*)..` (AR-03) and between the `infrastructure.(*)` sub-packages.
6. JPA annotations (`jakarta.persistence..`) appear only in `infrastructure.persistence`.

## 3. Conference configuration (AR-04, US-003, OQ-01, OQ-02)

A JSON file, schema [`02_contracts/conference-config.schema.json`](02_contracts/conference-config.schema.json). Path from setting `CONFERENCE_CONFIG_FILE`; when empty the backend uses the shipped `classpath:conference-config.json` (allowed in local and test only: with `APP_ENVIRONMENT=production` an empty path refuses start).

- `options[]`: `id` (pattern `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$`), `name` (non-blank), `category` (`WORKSHOP`, `EVENT`, `MEAL`, `OTHER`), `active` (default `true`), `availableTo` (non-empty subset of `EXTERNAL`, `STUDENT`; default both).
- `consents[]`: `id` (same pattern), `text` (non-blank), `mandatory` (default `true`). The shipped file has the `privacy` consent with the wording of OQ-02.
- Loaded once at start. Invalid file (unparseable, duplicate option or consent id, unknown category or type, missing or blank name/text, bad id) → the application context fails and the backend refuses to start (AC-003-03). Unknown properties are rejected too.
- Changing the file and restarting changes the form configuration without code changes (AC-003-02).

## 4. REST API (AR-09)

Exactly `api-contract.md`; machine-readable in `openapi.json`. Additions allowed by the contract: `GET /api/form-config` adds `captchaTestMode` (boolean); error responses other than 400 carry `{"message": "<general text>"}`.

| Endpoint | Access | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/form-config` | public, rate limited | active options only (AC-003-01), consents, `captchaSiteKey` (from `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`, may be empty in test mode), `captchaTestMode` |
| `POST /api/registrations` | public, rate limited, body ≤ `REQUEST_MAX_BYTES` | validation (§5) → captcha (§6) → store (§7) → emails (§8); 201 `{"id"}` |
| `GET /api/registrations` | organizer, rate limited | search (§9) |
| `GET /api/export` | organizer, rate limited | Excel workbook (§10) |

Status codes: 400 field errors `{"errors":[{"field","message"}]}` (also for malformed JSON: field `body`; wrong content type: 415 with `message`); 401 missing/wrong organizer credentials, body `{"message":"Authentication required"}`, `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="organizer"` unless the request carries `X-Requested-With` (so the organizer page gets no browser dialog); 403 organizer request over plain HTTP from a non-localhost client (D-10); 413 body too large; 429 over the rate limit with `Retry-After`; 500/503 `{"message":"…"}` without internals (SB-07) when storage or captcha verification fails.

## 5. Registration validation (BR-01..BR-05, SB-01, SR-04)

Server-side, in `domain`, collecting one error per invalid field (first problem per field):

| Field | Rule | Error field |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | required, `EXTERNAL` or `STUDENT` (unknown string → error, not a parse failure) | `type` |
| `firstName`, `lastName`, `email` | trimmed; non-empty; at most 200 characters (email 254) | same name |
| `email` | format `local@domain.tld`: no whitespace or control characters, exactly one `@`, a dot in the domain, no leading/trailing dot in the domain | `email` |
| `organization` | required for `EXTERNAL`, ignored (stored as null) for `STUDENT` | `organization` |
| `studyInstitution`, `studyProgramme`, `studentId` | required for `STUDENT`, ignored for `EXTERNAL` | same name |
| `options` | null treated as empty; each id is a configured, active option available to the type; no id twice; no null entry | `options` |
| `consents` | every mandatory consent present; unknown ids rejected; no id twice | `consents` |
| `captchaToken` | non-blank, then accepted by the verifier | `captchaToken` |

When the type is missing or unknown, only common fields are checked besides `type`. Validation runs before captcha verification; the captcha is verified only when every other field is valid, and a rejected token yields a `captchaToken` error. Text is stored trimmed (AC-001-03) and otherwise unchanged (Unicode, NFR-01). Duplicate emails are allowed (OQ-05).

## 6. reCAPTCHA (SR-01, SR-02, DoD-P05)

`CaptchaVerifier` port with two implementations chosen at start:

- Test mode (`CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=true`): only the token `test-pass` is accepted; no network call.
- Production path: HTTPS POST (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, `secret`, `response`) to `RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL` (default `https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api/siteverify`) with 5 s timeouts; accepted only if the JSON answer has `"success": true`. A network or parse failure → 503, nothing stored. Tested against a mocked endpoint (accepting and rejecting).
- Test mode is off unless configured. With test mode off, an empty `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` or `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` refuses start; with `APP_ENVIRONMENT=production`, test mode on refuses start.

Frontend: in test mode it sends `test-pass` without a widget and shows a "test mode" note; otherwise it loads the Google v2 widget with the site key and sends its token, and resets the widget after every response.

## 7. Storage (BR-07, AR-05, AR-06, ES-08, US-005)

Order inside `RegistrationService.register`, one database transaction:

1. Build the registration: new UUID, `registeredAt` = now truncated to milliseconds (UTC), each given consent with `givenAt` = `registeredAt`.
2. Insert the rows and flush.
3. Write the JSON copy `<id>.json` to `JSON_COPY_DIR`: written to a temporary file in the same directory, then atomically moved. Any failure throws → the transaction rolls back → 500, no row (AC-005-03).
4. Commit. If the commit fails, the JSON copy is deleted and the request fails.
5. Only then: 201 and emails (§8).

Schema (Flyway `V1__registration.sql`, AR-06): `registration` (`id uuid` PK, `seq bigserial` unique for stable newest-first order, `type`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `email`, `organization`, `study_institution`, `study_programme`, `student_id`, `search_text`, `registered_at timestamptz`), `registration_option` (`registration_id`, `position`, `option_id`), `registration_consent` (`registration_id`, `consent_id`, `given_at`). Text columns are `varchar` in a UTF-8 database. `search_text` holds the five searchable fields lower-cased with `Locale.ROOT` and joined by U+001F, so case-insensitive matching does not depend on the database collation (Slovenian characters, AC-009-11).

JSON copy: schema [`02_contracts/registration-copy.schema.json`](02_contracts/registration-copy.schema.json), UTF-8 without BOM: `id`, `type`, the eight participant fields (fields of the other type `null`), `options` (ids in submitted order), `consents` (`[{id, givenAt}]`), `registeredAt`.

## 8. Emails (US-006, US-007, SR-05, SR-07, OQ-03)

Sent synchronously after the commit through `Notifier` (Spring `JavaMailSender`; SMTP timeouts 5 s). Each send is caught separately: a failure is logged as `Email <kind> failed for registration <id>` with no personal data; the response stays 201 (AC-006-03).

- Participant: to the participant's address; subject `Registration confirmation: <CONFERENCE_NAME>`; `text/plain; charset=UTF-8` body naming the conference, the participant's name and the selected options by display name.
- Organizer: one message per address in `ORGANIZER_EMAILS`; subject `New registration <id>`; plain-text body with every submitted field, options, consents and time; attachment `registration-<id>.json` (`application/json`) whose bytes are exactly the JSON copy's bytes (AC-007-02). Only registration data (SR-07).
- Injection safety (AC-006-02): no user input in any header except the participant's validated address (no whitespace or control characters possible); plain-text bodies only, so markup stays literal.

Settings: `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_STARTTLS`, `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD`, `MAIL_FROM`, `CONFERENCE_NAME`, `ORGANIZER_EMAILS`.

## 9. Search (US-009, BR-09, BR-10)

`GET /api/registrations?text&type&option&page`, organizer only.

- Validation (AC-009-08): `text` more than 100 characters, raw (D-11) → `text`; `type` not `EXTERNAL`/`STUDENT` → `type`; `option` not a configured option id (active or inactive) → `option`; `page` not an integer ≥ 1 → `page`. Empty parameters count as absent.
- Matching: text trimmed, lower-cased (`Locale.ROOT`), U+001F removed; `search_text LIKE %text%` with `\`, `%`, `_` escaped; empty text matches all. Type and option filters combine with AND (AC-009-05).
- Order `registered_at DESC, seq DESC`; page size 20; `total` = number of matches; a page past the end gives an empty `items`.
- Item fields: `id`, `type`, `firstName`, `lastName`, `email`, `organization`, `studyInstitution`, `options`, `registeredAt`.

## 10. Export (US-008, BR-08, SR-07)

`GET /api/export`, organizer only: XSSF workbook, sheet `Registrations`, header row exactly the contract's 12 columns, one row per registration ordered oldest first; all cells are string cells (no formulas, so cell text starting with `=` is not evaluated); `options`/`consents` joined with `, `; cells of the other type empty; `registeredAt` ISO 8601. `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="registrations.xlsx"`.

## 11. Security (SB-01..SB-14, SR-01..SR-09)

- Organizer authentication (BR-08, BR-09, SB-02, SB-03): Spring Security HTTP Basic on `GET /api/registrations` and `GET /api/export`; one in-memory user from `ORGANIZER_USERNAME`/`ORGANIZER_PASSWORD`, password hashed with BCrypt at start and only the hash kept. Stateless, no session, CSRF off (no cookies, no ambient credentials). Everything else under `/api` is public; `/actuator/health/**` public; all other paths denied.

Client address and scheme come from the connection, or from `X-Forwarded-For`/`X-Forwarded-Proto` only when the connection comes from a trusted proxy (`TRUSTED_PROXIES`, a regular expression of proxy IPs, default none: Tomcat `RemoteIpValve`). `APP_ENVIRONMENT=production` refuses start with `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY=false`.

Request bodies over `REQUEST_MAX_BYTES` (default 16384) → 413 (by `Content-Length` and by counting a body without length).

- Output encoding (SB-05, SR-09): React renders participant data as text, never as HTML (`dangerouslySetInnerHTML` not used); JPA parameterised queries only; emails plain text; Excel string cells.
- Errors and logs (SB-07, ES-07): global handler maps every unexpected exception to a general message; logs carry registration ids, never personal data or secrets.

- Least privilege (SB-11): both images run as non-root users.
- Personal data (SB-12..SB-14): only the fields of BR-01's Data table, consents with time; retention per OQ-06 in the release notes; consents never preselected (BR-05).

UI contract: [`02_contracts/ui-contract.md`](02_contracts/ui-contract.md). Routes by path: `/` registration, `/organizer` organizer search page (nginx falls back to `index.html`).

- Registration page: loads `/api/form-config`; a choice "External participant" / "Student"; after the choice exactly that type's fields, the options available to the type grouped under Workshops, Events, Meals, Other activities (empty groups hidden), unchecked consent checkboxes, the captcha, a "Register" button.

# Specification

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: `project/01_requirements/*`, `project/02_design/*`, `project/00_setup/tech-stack.md`, `project/00_setup/environments.md`, `general/security/*` · Agent: writes

Conference registration: a public registration form (external participants and students), storage in PostgreSQL plus a raw JSON copy, confirmation and organizer emails, an organizer Excel export and an organizer search page. The REST API is fixed by `api-contract.md` (AR-09) and described exactly by [`02_contracts/openapi.json`](02_contracts/openapi.json).

## 1. Components and runtime

| Component | Folder | Runs as | Talks to |
|---|---|---|---|
| backend | `02_output/backend` | Spring Boot jar in `eclipse-temurin` JRE image, non-root user, port 8080 | PostgreSQL (JDBC), SMTP, reCAPTCHA verify endpoint (HTTPS), JSON copy directory |
| frontend | `02_output/frontend` | React SPA built by Vite, served by `nginx` (non-root, port 8080), which also proxies `/api` to the backend | backend only through `/api` (AR-01) |
| postgres | image | `postgres` 16 with named volume `pgdata` | – |
| mailpit | image | local SMTP catcher (SMTP 1025, web/API 8025) | – |

Local stack: `02_output/docker-compose.yml`. Published on 127.0.0.1 only: backend `8080`, frontend `8081`, Mailpit `8025`. Named volumes `pgdata` and `jsoncopies` keep data across container recreation (NFR-02). Production: the same two images behind an external nginx that terminates TLS, serves `/` from the frontend and forwards `/api` to the backend with a fixed upstream `Host` (SR-08); a sample is in the backend README.

## 2. Backend architecture (AR-02, AR-03)

Ports-and-adapters with four layers under `si.konferenca.registration`:

| Package | Contents | May depend on |
|---|---|---|
| `domain` | registration model, types, option and consent definitions, conference configuration model, validation rules, search criteria, field errors | `java.*` only |
| `application` | use cases (`RegistrationService`, `SearchService`, `ExportService`) and the ports they need (`RegistrationStore`, `JsonCopyStore`, `CaptchaVerifier`, `Notifier`, `WorkbookWriter`) | `domain`, Spring stereotypes and transactions |
| `infrastructure.*` | adapters implementing the ports: `persistence` (JPA), `jsoncopy` (files), `mail` (SMTP), `captcha` (reCAPTCHA), `excel` (POI), `config` (options file loading, settings, startup checks) | `application`, `domain`, frameworks |
| `web` | REST controllers, request/response DTOs, error mapping, rate limit and body size filters | `application`, `domain` |
| `security` | Spring Security configuration, organizer authentication, HTTPS-only filter, headers, CORS | `domain`, `infrastructure.config` (settings), frameworks |

Justification: the business rules (validation, option availability, search semantics) are the code that must be mutation-tested most and change least; keeping them framework-free in `domain` makes them unit-testable and keeps the frameworks replaceable at the edges. `application` holds the one place where the storage order of BR-07/AR-05 is decided.

ArchUnit rules (written in phase 5, they check exactly this table):

1. `domain` depends only on `java..` classes.
2. `application` does not depend on `infrastructure..`, `web..` or `security..`.
3. `web` does not depend on `infrastructure..`.
4. `infrastructure..` does not depend on `web..` or `security..`.
5. No cycles between the slices `si.konferenca.registration.(*)..` (AR-03) and between the `infrastructure.(*)` sub-packages.
6. JPA annotations (`jakarta.persistence..`) appear only in `infrastructure.persistence`.

## 3. Conference configuration (AR-04, US-003, OQ-01, OQ-02)

A JSON file, schema [`02_contracts/conference-config.schema.json`](02_contracts/conference-config.schema.json). Path from setting `CONFERENCE_CONFIG_FILE`; when empty the backend uses the shipped `classpath:conference-config.json` (allowed in local and test only: with `APP_ENVIRONMENT=production` an empty path refuses start).

- `options[]`: `id` (pattern `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$`), `name` (non-blank), `category` (`WORKSHOP`, `EVENT`, `MEAL`, `OTHER`), `active` (default `true`), `availableTo` (non-empty subset of `EXTERNAL`, `STUDENT`; default both).
- `consents[]`: `id` (same pattern), `text` (non-blank), `mandatory` (default `true`). The shipped file has the `privacy` consent with the wording of OQ-02.
- Loaded once at start. Invalid file (unparseable, duplicate option or consent id, unknown category or type, missing or blank name/text, bad id) → the application context fails and the backend refuses to start (AC-003-03). Unknown properties are rejected too.
- Changing the file and restarting changes the form configuration without code changes (AC-003-02).

## 4. REST API (AR-09)

Exactly `api-contract.md`; machine-readable in `openapi.json`. Additions allowed by the contract: `GET /api/form-config` adds `captchaTestMode` (boolean); error responses other than 400 carry `{"message": "<general text>"}`.

| Endpoint | Access | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/form-config` | public, rate limited | active options only (AC-003-01), consents, `captchaSiteKey` (from `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`, may be empty in test mode), `captchaTestMode` |
| `POST /api/registrations` | public, rate limited, body ≤ `REQUEST_MAX_BYTES` | validation (§5) → captcha (§6) → store (§7) → emails (§8); 201 `{"id"}` |
| `GET /api/registrations` | organizer, rate limited | search (§9) |
| `GET /api/export` | organizer, rate limited | Excel workbook (§10) |

Status codes: 400 field errors `{"errors":[{"field","message"}]}` (also for malformed JSON: field `body`; wrong content type: 415 with `message`); 401 missing/wrong organizer credentials, body `{"message":"Authentication required"}`, `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="organizer"` unless the request carries `X-Requested-With` (so the organizer page gets no browser dialog); 403 organizer request over plain HTTP from a non-localhost client (D-10); 413 body too large; 429 over the rate limit with `Retry-After`; 500/503 `{"message":"…"}` without internals (SB-07) when storage or captcha verification fails.

## 5. Registration validation (BR-01..BR-05, SB-01, SR-04)

Server-side, in `domain`, collecting one error per invalid field (first problem per field):

| Field | Rule | Error field |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | required, `EXTERNAL` or `STUDENT` (unknown string → error, not a parse failure) | `type` |
| `firstName`, `lastName`, `email` | trimmed; non-empty; at most 200 characters (email 254) | same name |
| `email` | format `local@domain.tld`: no whitespace or control characters, exactly one `@`, a dot in the domain, no leading/trailing dot in the domain | `email` |
| `organization` | required for `EXTERNAL`, ignored (stored as null) for `STUDENT` | `organization` |
| `studyInstitution`, `studyProgramme`, `studentId` | required for `STUDENT`, ignored for `EXTERNAL` | same name |
| `options` | null treated as empty; each id is a configured, active option available to the type; no id twice; no null entry | `options` |
| `consents` | every mandatory consent present; unknown ids rejected; no id twice | `consents` |
| `captchaToken` | non-blank, then accepted by the verifier | `captchaToken` |

When the type is missing or unknown, only common fields are checked besides `type`. Validation runs before captcha verification; the captcha is verified only when every other field is valid, and a rejected token yields a `captchaToken` error. Text is stored trimmed (AC-001-03) and otherwise unchanged (Unicode, NFR-01). Duplicate emails are allowed (OQ-05).

## 6. reCAPTCHA (SR-01, SR-02, DoD-P05)

`CaptchaVerifier` port with two implementations chosen at start:

- Test mode (`CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=true`): only the token `test-pass` is accepted; no network call.
- Production path: HTTPS POST (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, `secret`, `response`) to `RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL` (default `https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api/siteverify`) with 5 s timeouts; accepted only if the JSON answer has `"success": true`. A network or parse failure → 503, nothing stored. Tested against a mocked endpoint (accepting and rejecting).
- Test mode is off unless configured. With test mode off, an empty `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` or `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` refuses start; with `APP_ENVIRONMENT=production`, test mode on refuses start.

Frontend: in test mode it sends `test-pass` without a widget and shows a "test mode" note; otherwise it loads the Google v2 widget with the site key and sends its token, and resets the widget after every response.

## 7. Storage (BR-07, AR-05, AR-06, ES-08, US-005)

Order inside `RegistrationService.register`, one database transaction:

1. Build the registration: new UUID, `registeredAt` = now truncated to milliseconds (UTC), each given consent with `givenAt` = `registeredAt`.
2. Insert the rows and flush.
3. Write the JSON copy `<id>.json` to `JSON_COPY_DIR`: written to a temporary file in the same directory, then atomically moved. Any failure throws → the transaction rolls back → 500, no row (AC-005-03).
4. Commit. If the commit fails, the JSON copy is deleted and the request fails.
5. Only then: 201 and emails (§8).

Schema (Flyway `V1__registration.sql`, AR-06): `registration` (`id uuid` PK, `seq bigserial` unique for stable newest-first order, `type`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `email`, `organization`, `study_institution`, `study_programme`, `student_id`, `search_text`, `registered_at timestamptz`), `registration_option` (`registration_id`, `position`, `option_id`), `registration_consent` (`registration_id`, `consent_id`, `given_at`). Text columns are `varchar` in a UTF-8 database. `search_text` holds the five searchable fields lower-cased with `Locale.ROOT` and joined by U+001F, so case-insensitive matching does not depend on the database collation (Slovenian characters, AC-009-11).

JSON copy: schema [`02_contracts/registration-copy.schema.json`](02_contracts/registration-copy.schema.json), UTF-8 without BOM: `id`, `type`, the eight participant fields (fields of the other type `null`), `options` (ids in submitted order), `consents` (`[{id, givenAt}]`), `registeredAt`.

## 8. Emails (US-006, US-007, SR-05, SR-07, OQ-03)

Sent synchronously after the commit through `Notifier` (Spring `JavaMailSender`; SMTP timeouts 5 s). Each send is caught separately: a failure is logged as `Email <kind> failed for registration <id>` with no personal data; the response stays 201 (AC-006-03).

- Participant: to the participant's address; subject `Registration confirmation: <CONFERENCE_NAME>`; `text/plain; charset=UTF-8` body naming the conference, the participant's name and the selected options by display name.
- Organizer: one message per address in `ORGANIZER_EMAILS`; subject `New registration <id>`; plain-text body with every submitted field, options, consents and time; attachment `registration-<id>.json` (`application/json`) whose bytes are exactly the JSON copy's bytes (AC-007-02). Only registration data (SR-07).
- Injection safety (AC-006-02): no user input in any header except the participant's validated address (no whitespace or control characters possible); plain-text bodies only, so markup stays literal.

Settings: `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_STARTTLS`, `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD`, `MAIL_FROM`, `CONFERENCE_NAME`, `ORGANIZER_EMAILS`.

## 9. Search (US-009, BR-09, BR-10)

`GET /api/registrations?text&type&option&page`, organizer only.

- Validation (AC-009-08): `text` more than 100 characters, raw (D-11) → `text`; `type` not `EXTERNAL`/`STUDENT` → `type`; `option` not a configured option id (active or inactive) → `option`; `page` not an integer ≥ 1 → `page`. Empty parameters count as absent.
- Matching: text trimmed, lower-cased (`Locale.ROOT`), U+001F removed; `search_text LIKE %text%` with `\`, `%`, `_` escaped; empty text matches all. Type and option filters combine with AND (AC-009-05).
- Order `registered_at DESC, seq DESC`; page size 20; `total` = number of matches; a page past the end gives an empty `items`.
- Item fields: `id`, `type`, `firstName`, `lastName`, `email`, `organization`, `studyInstitution`, `options`, `registeredAt`.

## 10. Export (US-008, BR-08, SR-07)

`GET /api/export`, organizer only: XSSF workbook, sheet `Registrations`, header row exactly the contract's 12 columns, one row per registration ordered oldest first; all cells are string cells (no formulas, so cell text starting with `=` is not evaluated); `options`/`consents` joined with `, `; cells of the other type empty; `registeredAt` ISO 8601. `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="registrations.xlsx"`.

# Specification

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: `project/01_requirements/*`, `project/02_design/*`, `project/00_setup/tech-stack.md`, `project/00_setup/environments.md`, `general/security/*` · Agent: writes

Conference registration: a public registration form (external participants and students), storage in PostgreSQL plus a raw JSON copy, confirmation and organizer emails, an organizer Excel export and an organizer search page. The REST API is fixed by `api-contract.md` (AR-09) and described exactly by [`02_contracts/openapi.json`](02_contracts/openapi.json).

## 1. Components and runtime

| Component | Folder | Runs as | Talks to |
|---|---|---|---|
| backend | `02_output/backend` | Spring Boot jar in `eclipse-temurin` JRE image, non-root user, port 8080 | PostgreSQL (JDBC), SMTP, reCAPTCHA verify endpoint (HTTPS), JSON copy directory |
| frontend | `02_output/frontend` | React SPA built by Vite, served by `nginx` (non-root, port 8080), which also proxies `/api` to the backend | backend only through `/api` (AR-01) |
| postgres | image | `postgres` 16 with named volume `pgdata` | – |
| mailpit | image | local SMTP catcher (SMTP 1025, web/API 8025) | – |

Local stack: `02_output/docker-compose.yml`. Published on 127.0.0.1 only: backend `8080`, frontend `8081`, Mailpit `8025`. Named volumes `pgdata` and `jsoncopies` keep data across container recreation (NFR-02). Production: the same two images behind an external nginx that terminates TLS, serves `/` from the frontend and forwards `/api` to the backend with a fixed upstream `Host` (SR-08); a sample is in the backend README.

## 2. Backend architecture (AR-02, AR-03)

Ports-and-adapters with four layers under `si.konferenca.registration`:

| Package | Contents | May depend on |
|---|---|---|
| `domain` | registration model, types, option and consent definitions, conference configuration model, validation rules, search criteria, field errors | `java.*` only |
| `application` | use cases (`RegistrationService`, `SearchService`, `ExportService`) and the ports they need (`RegistrationStore`, `JsonCopyStore`, `CaptchaVerifier`, `Notifier`, `WorkbookWriter`) | `domain`, Spring stereotypes and transactions |
| `infrastructure.*` | adapters implementing the ports: `persistence` (JPA), `jsoncopy` (files), `mail` (SMTP), `captcha` (reCAPTCHA), `excel` (POI), `config` (options file loading, settings, startup checks) | `application`, `domain`, frameworks |
| `web` | REST controllers, request/response DTOs, error mapping, rate limit and body size filters | `application`, `domain` |
| `security` | Spring Security configuration, organizer authentication, HTTPS-only filter, headers, CORS | `domain`, `infrastructure.config` (settings), frameworks |

Justification: the business rules (validation, option availability, search semantics) are the code that must be mutation-tested most and change least; keeping them framework-free in `domain` makes them unit-testable and keeps the frameworks replaceable at the edges. `application` holds the one place where the storage order of BR-07/AR-05 is decided.

ArchUnit rules (written in phase 5, they check exactly this table):

1. `domain` depends only on `java..` classes.
2. `application` does not depend on `infrastructure..`, `web..` or `security..`.
3. `web` does not depend on `infrastructure..`.
4. `infrastructure..` does not depend on `web..` or `security..`.
5. No cycles between the slices `si.konferenca.registration.(*)..` (AR-03) and between the `infrastructure.(*)` sub-packages.
6. JPA annotations (`jakarta.persistence..`) appear only in `infrastructure.persistence`.

## 3. Conference configuration (AR-04, US-003, OQ-01, OQ-02)

A JSON file, schema [`02_contracts/conference-config.schema.json`](02_contracts/conference-config.schema.json). Path from setting `CONFERENCE_CONFIG_FILE`; when empty the backend uses the shipped `classpath:conference-config.json` (allowed in local and test only: with `APP_ENVIRONMENT=production` an empty path refuses start).

- `options[]`: `id` (pattern `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$`), `name` (non-blank), `category` (`WORKSHOP`, `EVENT`, `MEAL`, `OTHER`), `active` (default `true`), `availableTo` (non-empty subset of `EXTERNAL`, `STUDENT`; default both).
- `consents[]`: `id` (same pattern), `text` (non-blank), `mandatory` (default `true`). The shipped file has the `privacy` consent with the wording of OQ-02.
- Loaded once at start. Invalid file (unparseable, duplicate option or consent id, unknown category or type, missing or blank name/text, bad id) → the application context fails and the backend refuses to start (AC-003-03). Unknown properties are rejected too.
- Changing the file and restarting changes the form configuration without code changes (AC-003-02).

## 4. REST API (AR-09)

Exactly `api-contract.md`; machine-readable in `openapi.json`. Additions allowed by the contract: `GET /api/form-config` adds `captchaTestMode` (boolean); error responses other than 400 carry `{"message": "<general text>"}`.

| Endpoint | Access | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/form-config` | public, rate limited | active options only (AC-003-01), consents, `captchaSiteKey` (from `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`, may be empty in test mode), `captchaTestMode` |
| `POST /api/registrations` | public, rate limited, body ≤ `REQUEST_MAX_BYTES` | validation (§5) → captcha (§6) → store (§7) → emails (§8); 201 `{"id"}` |
| `GET /api/registrations` | organizer, rate limited | search (§9) |
| `GET /api/export` | organizer, rate limited | Excel workbook (§10) |

Status codes: 400 field errors `{"errors":[{"field","message"}]}` (also for malformed JSON: field `body`; wrong content type: 415 with `message`); 401 missing/wrong organizer credentials, body `{"message":"Authentication required"}`, `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="organizer"` unless the request carries `X-Requested-With` (so the organizer page gets no browser dialog); 403 organizer request over plain HTTP from a non-localhost client (D-10); 413 body too large; 429 over the rate limit with `Retry-After`; 500/503 `{"message":"…"}` without internals (SB-07) when storage or captcha verification fails.

## 5. Registration validation (BR-01..BR-05, SB-01, SR-04)

Server-side, in `domain`, collecting one error per invalid field (first problem per field):

| Field | Rule | Error field |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | required, `EXTERNAL` or `STUDENT` (unknown string → error, not a parse failure) | `type` |
| `firstName`, `lastName`, `email` | trimmed; non-empty; at most 200 characters (email 254) | same name |
| `email` | format `local@domain.tld`: no whitespace or control characters, exactly one `@`, a dot in the domain, no leading/trailing dot in the domain | `email` |
| `organization` | required for `EXTERNAL`, ignored (stored as null) for `STUDENT` | `organization` |
| `studyInstitution`, `studyProgramme`, `studentId` | required for `STUDENT`, ignored for `EXTERNAL` | same name |
| `options` | null treated as empty; each id is a configured, active option available to the type; no id twice; no null entry | `options` |
| `consents` | every mandatory consent present; unknown ids rejected; no id twice | `consents` |
| `captchaToken` | non-blank, then accepted by the verifier | `captchaToken` |

When the type is missing or unknown, only common fields are checked besides `type`. Validation runs before captcha verification; the captcha is verified only when every other field is valid, and a rejected token yields a `captchaToken` error. Text is stored trimmed (AC-001-03) and otherwise unchanged (Unicode, NFR-01). Duplicate emails are allowed (OQ-05).

## 6. reCAPTCHA (SR-01, SR-02, DoD-P05)

`CaptchaVerifier` port with two implementations chosen at start:

- Test mode (`CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=true`): only the token `test-pass` is accepted; no network call.
- Production path: HTTPS POST (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, `secret`, `response`) to `RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL` (default `https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api/siteverify`) with 5 s timeouts; accepted only if the JSON answer has `"success": true`. A network or parse failure → 503, nothing stored. Tested against a mocked endpoint (accepting and rejecting).
- Test mode is off unless configured. With test mode off, an empty `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` or `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` refuses start; with `APP_ENVIRONMENT=production`, test mode on refuses start.

Frontend: in test mode it sends `test-pass` without a widget and shows a "test mode" note; otherwise it loads the Google v2 widget with the site key and sends its token, and resets the widget after every response.

## 7. Storage (BR-07, AR-05, AR-06, ES-08, US-005)

Order inside `RegistrationService.register`, one database transaction:

1. Build the registration: new UUID, `registeredAt` = now truncated to milliseconds (UTC), each given consent with `givenAt` = `registeredAt`.
2. Insert the rows and flush.
3. Write the JSON copy `<id>.json` to `JSON_COPY_DIR`: written to a temporary file in the same directory, then atomically moved. Any failure throws → the transaction rolls back → 500, no row (AC-005-03).
4. Commit. If the commit fails, the JSON copy is deleted and the request fails.
5. Only then: 201 and emails (§8).

Schema (Flyway `V1__registration.sql`, AR-06): `registration` (`id uuid` PK, `seq bigserial` unique for stable newest-first order, `type`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `email`, `organization`, `study_institution`, `study_programme`, `student_id`, `search_text`, `registered_at timestamptz`), `registration_option` (`registration_id`, `position`, `option_id`), `registration_consent` (`registration_id`, `consent_id`, `given_at`). Text columns are `varchar` in a UTF-8 database. `search_text` holds the five searchable fields lower-cased with `Locale.ROOT` and joined by U+001F, so case-insensitive matching does not depend on the database collation (Slovenian characters, AC-009-11).

JSON copy: schema [`02_contracts/registration-copy.schema.json`](02_contracts/registration-copy.schema.json), UTF-8 without BOM: `id`, `type`, the eight participant fields (fields of the other type `null`), `options` (ids in submitted order), `consents` (`[{id, givenAt}]`), `registeredAt`.

## 8. Emails (US-006, US-007, SR-05, SR-07, OQ-03)

Sent synchronously after the commit through `Notifier` (Spring `JavaMailSender`; SMTP timeouts 5 s). Each send is caught separately: a failure is logged as `Email <kind> failed for registration <id>` with no personal data; the response stays 201 (AC-006-03).

- Participant: to the participant's address; subject `Registration confirmation: <CONFERENCE_NAME>`; `text/plain; charset=UTF-8` body naming the conference, the participant's name and the selected options by display name.
- Organizer: one message per address in `ORGANIZER_EMAILS`; subject `New registration <id>`; plain-text body with every submitted field, options, consents and time; attachment `registration-<id>.json` (`application/json`) whose bytes are exactly the JSON copy's bytes (AC-007-02). Only registration data (SR-07).
- Injection safety (AC-006-02): no user input in any header except the participant's validated address (no whitespace or control characters possible); plain-text bodies only, so markup stays literal.

Settings: `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_STARTTLS`, `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD`, `MAIL_FROM`, `CONFERENCE_NAME`, `ORGANIZER_EMAILS`.

## 9. Search (US-009, BR-09, BR-10)

`GET /api/registrations?text&type&option&page`, organizer only.

- Validation (AC-009-08): `text` more than 100 characters, raw (D-11) → `text`; `type` not `EXTERNAL`/`STUDENT` → `type`; `option` not a configured option id (active or inactive) → `option`; `page` not an integer ≥ 1 → `page`. Empty parameters count as absent.
- Matching: text trimmed, lower-cased (`Locale.ROOT`), U+001F removed; `search_text LIKE %text%` with `\`, `%`, `_` escaped; empty text matches all. Type and option filters combine with AND (AC-009-05).
- Order `registered_at DESC, seq DESC`; page size 20; `total` = number of matches; a page past the end gives an empty `items`.
- Item fields: `id`, `type`, `firstName`, `lastName`, `email`, `organization`, `studyInstitution`, `options`, `registeredAt`.

## 10. Export (US-008, BR-08, SR-07)

`GET /api/export`, organizer only: XSSF workbook, sheet `Registrations`, header row exactly the contract's 12 columns, one row per registration ordered oldest first; all cells are string cells (no formulas, so cell text starting with `=` is not evaluated); `options`/`consents` joined with `, `; cells of the other type empty; `registeredAt` ISO 8601. `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="registrations.xlsx"`.

## 11. Security (SB-01..SB-14, SR-01..SR-09)

- Organizer authentication (BR-08, BR-09, SB-02, SB-03): Spring Security HTTP Basic on `GET /api/registrations` and `GET /api/export`; one in-memory user from `ORGANIZER_USERNAME`/`ORGANIZER_PASSWORD`, password hashed with BCrypt at start and only the hash kept. Stateless, no session, CSRF off (no cookies, no ambient credentials). Everything else under `/api` is public; `/actuator/health/**` public; all other paths denied.
- HTTPS only (SR-06, `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY`, default `true`): an organizer request that is not secure and does not come from a loopback address is refused with 403 before authentication (D-10). Client address and scheme come from the connection, or from `X-Forwarded-For`/`X-Forwarded-Proto` only when the connection comes from a trusted proxy (`TRUSTED_PROXIES`, a regular expression of proxy IPs, default none: Tomcat `RemoteIpValve`). `APP_ENVIRONMENT=production` refuses start with `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY=false`.
- Rate limits (SR-03, SB-06): fixed one-minute window per client address and endpoint (method + path) for every `/api` endpoint; limit `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` (default 60); over the limit → 429 with `Retry-After`. Request bodies over `REQUEST_MAX_BYTES` (default 16384) → 413 (by `Content-Length` and by counting a body without length).
- Headers (SB-10): backend sends `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `Cache-Control: no-store`. The frontend nginx sends a CSP allowing only self plus the Google reCAPTCHA script and frame origins, `frame-ancestors 'none'`, nosniff and `Referrer-Policy`.
- CORS: off unless `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGIN` is set (local development only; production refuses start with it set).
- Output encoding (SB-05, SR-09): React renders participant data as text, never as HTML (`dangerouslySetInnerHTML` not used); JPA parameterised queries only; emails plain text; Excel string cells.
- Errors and logs (SB-07, ES-07): global handler maps every unexpected exception to a general message; logs carry registration ids, never personal data or secrets.
- Proxy `Host` (SR-08): the frontend nginx and the documented production nginx set the upstream `Host` themselves (`proxy_set_header Host backend:8080` / the upstream name), never `$host`/`$http_host`.
- Least privilege (SB-11): both images run as non-root users.
- Personal data (SB-12..SB-14): only the fields of BR-01's Data table, consents with time; retention per OQ-06 in the release notes; consents never preselected (BR-05).
- Dependencies and source scanning (SB-08, SB-09): Dependency-Check, `npm audit`, Semgrep, Gitleaks in phase 6.

UI contract: [`02_contracts/ui-contract.md`](02_contracts/ui-contract.md). Routes by path: `/` registration, `/organizer` organizer search page (nginx falls back to `index.html`).

- Backend 400: each error next to its field; values kept (AC-004-02); errors for fields without an input (`type`, `captchaToken`, `body`) in the form's error area.
- 201: a confirmation with the participant's name and selected option names replaces the form (AC-004-01, BR-06).
- Any other status or network failure: a general message without technical details; no confirmation (AC-004-04).
- Organizer page: username/password form; credentials kept in memory only and sent as Basic with `X-Requested-With`; wrong credentials → error and no data; then a search field with a Search button, type filter (All, External, Student), option filter (All + configured options from form-config), a table of results, total, page navigation (Previous/Next, "Page n of m").
