# Conference registration

> Written in: phase 7 · Source: `project/02_design/architecture.md`, ES-06 · Agent: writes

## Overview

Online registration for a conference: external participants and students register through a web form, choose workshops, events, meals and other activities from a configurable list, and give the required consent. Every accepted registration is stored in PostgreSQL and as a raw JSON copy, confirmed to the participant by email and announced to the organizers by email with the JSON copy attached. Organizers search and filter registrations on an organizer page and export them as an Excel workbook.

## Components

| Component | Folder | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| backend | [backend/](backend/README.md) | Spring Boot REST API (`/api`), PostgreSQL via Flyway, JSON copies, emails, reCAPTCHA, organizer access |
| frontend | [frontend/](frontend/README.md) | React single-page app (registration form at `/`, organizer page at `/organizer`) served by nginx, which forwards `/api` to the backend |

The local stack (`docker-compose.yml`) runs both components with PostgreSQL and Mailpit (a local mail catcher).

## Quick start

Prerequisites: Docker Engine with Docker Compose, and a `.env` file at the repository root (one level above this folder):

1. Copy `01_input/01_project/00_setup/secrets.env.example` to `.env` at the repository root and fill in `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `ORGANIZER_USERNAME`, `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` (16+ characters) and `ORGANIZER_EMAILS`. The reCAPTCHA and SMTP keys stay empty locally.
2. Start everything from this folder:

   ```bash
   cd 02_output
   docker compose --env-file ../.env up -d --build
   ```

3. Open:
   - registration form: <http://127.0.0.1:8081/>
   - organizer page: <http://127.0.0.1:8081/organizer> (the organizer credentials from `.env`)
   - emails (Mailpit): <http://127.0.0.1:8025/>
   - API: <http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/form-config>, health <http://127.0.0.1:8080/actuator/health>

4. Stop with `docker compose --env-file ../.env down` (data stays in the named volumes `pgdata` and `jsoncopies`; add `-v` to delete it).

Locally reCAPTCHA runs in test mode (`CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=true`, the form sends the token `test-pass`), organizer access over plain HTTP is allowed (`ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY=false`), and the API allows 60 requests per minute per client and endpoint (`RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE`). All three can be overridden when starting, for example `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE=1000 docker compose --env-file ../.env up -d`.

## Tests

| What | Command | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| backend unit, architecture and acceptance tests | `cd backend && ./mvnw verify` | Docker (Testcontainers) |
| frontend unit and acceptance tests | `cd frontend && npm ci && npm test` | Node |
| end-to-end tests (browser) | `cd frontend && npm run e2e` | the running local stack above |

## Documentation

| Document | Content |
|---|---|
| [docs/02_specification.md](docs/02_specification.md) | architecture, behaviour, settings, traceability |
| [docs/02_contracts/](docs/02_contracts/) | OpenAPI contract, JSON schemas, email and UI contracts |
| [docs/03_test-strategy.md](docs/03_test-strategy.md) | test levels, coverage and mutation results |
| [docs/06_verification-report.md](docs/06_verification-report.md) | verification evidence and findings |
| [docs/release-notes.md](docs/release-notes.md) | release notes and manual tests |
| [docs/decisions-log.md](docs/decisions-log.md) | decisions taken during the build |

# Backend

> Written in: phase 7 · Source: `project/02_design/architecture.md`, ES-05, ES-06 · Agent: writes

Spring Boot REST API of the conference registration (`/api`, contract in [`../docs/02_contracts/openapi.json`](../docs/02_contracts/openapi.json)). Root package `si.konferenca.registration`: `domain` (rules), `application` (use cases and ports), `infrastructure` (database, JSON copies, mail, reCAPTCHA, Excel, configuration), `web` (controllers), `security` (organizer access, HTTPS-only, rate and size limits).

## Prerequisites

- JDK 21 (the Maven wrapper downloads Maven 3.9.9; nothing else to install)
- Docker, for the tests (Testcontainers starts PostgreSQL and Mailpit) and for the container image

## Commands (ES-05)

| Purpose | Command |
|---|---|
| build | `./mvnw -B package -DskipTests` (jar in `target/`) |
| test | `./mvnw -B verify` (all tests; coverage report in `target/site/jacoco/`) |
| check | `./mvnw -B spotless:check compile pmd:check pmd:cpd-check spotbugs:check` |
| run (local stack) | `docker compose --env-file ../.env up -d --build` in `02_output/` |
| run (jar, against your own PostgreSQL and SMTP) | set the settings below as environment variables, then `java -jar target/registration-backend-1.0.0.jar` |
| mutation score | `./mvnw -B test-compile org.pitest:pitest-maven:1.30.0:mutationCoverage` (report in `target/pit-reports/`, about 30 minutes) |
| dependency scan | `NVD_API_KEY=… ./mvnw -B org.owasp:dependency-check-maven:12.1.0:check` |

On Windows use `mvnw.cmd`.

## Configuration

Every environment-specific value is a setting (environment variable); secrets have no default.

| Setting | Default | Source / notes |
|---|---|---|
| `SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL`, `SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME` | `jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/registration`, `registration` | compose sets them |
| `SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD` | none | secret `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` from `.env` |
| `SPRING_MAIL_HOST`, `SPRING_MAIL_PORT` | `localhost`, `1025` | SMTP server; compose uses Mailpit |
| `SPRING_MAIL_USERNAME`, `SPRING_MAIL_PASSWORD`, `SMTP_STARTTLS` | empty, empty, `false` | production SMTP account (secrets `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD`) |
| `MAIL_FROM`, `CONFERENCE_NAME` | `registration@konferenca.si`, `Conference` | sender and conference name in emails |
| `ORGANIZER_USERNAME`, `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` | none | secrets from `.env`; the password is kept only as a BCrypt hash |
| `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` | empty | comma-separated notification recipients |
| `CONFERENCE_CONFIG_FILE` | shipped `conference-config.json` | options and consents (schema [`../docs/02_contracts/conference-config.schema.json`](../docs/02_contracts/conference-config.schema.json)); required in production |

| `CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE` | `false` | `true` accepts only the token `test-pass` (local and test only) |
| `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`, `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` | empty | required unless test mode |
| `RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL` | Google siteverify URL | |
| `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY` | `true` | organizer requests over plain HTTP from other hosts get 403 |
| `TRUSTED_PROXIES` | none | regular expression of proxy IP addresses whose `X-Forwarded-For`/`-Proto` are trusted |
| `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE`, `REQUEST_MAX_BYTES` | `60`, `16384` | per client and endpoint; request body limit |
| `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGIN` | empty | local development only |
| `APP_ENVIRONMENT` | `local` | `production` refuses to start with test mode, plain-HTTP organizer access, CORS or no options file |

Changing the options: edit the configuration file (or point `CONFERENCE_CONFIG_FILE` to another one) and restart; an invalid file stops the start with a message naming the problem.

## Production reverse proxy (SR-08)

The backend container listens on HTTP 8080 behind an nginx that terminates TLS. The proxy sets the upstream `Host` itself and the backend trusts only its address:

```nginx
location /api/ {
    proxy_pass http://backend:8080;
    proxy_set_header Host backend:8080;          # never $host or $http_host
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
}
```

Start the backend with `APP_ENVIRONMENT=production`, `TRUSTED_PROXIES=<nginx IP as regex>`, real reCAPTCHA keys and SMTP settings.

## Health

`/actuator/health`, `/actuator/health/liveness`, `/actuator/health/readiness` (readiness includes the database; a mail outage does not make the backend unready).

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause and fix |
|---|---|
| start fails with "Could not resolve placeholder 'ORGANIZER_USERNAME'" | the organizer secrets are missing; set them (compose reads them from `.env`) |
| start fails with "Refusing to start: …" | the message names the unsafe setting (for example reCAPTCHA keys missing without test mode) |
| start fails with "Invalid conference configuration: …" | fix the named problem in the options file |
| tests fail with "Could not find a valid Docker environment" | start Docker; Testcontainers needs it |
| registrations answer 500 | the JSON copy directory is not writable; check `JSON_COPY_DIR` and the volume |
| 429 answers | over `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` for one client and endpoint; raise it for load tests |

# Frontend

> Written in: phase 7 · Source: `project/02_design/architecture.md`, ES-05, ES-06 · Agent: writes

React single-page app built with Vite: the registration form at `/` and the organizer search page at `/organizer`. It talks to the backend only through `/api` (AR-01); in the container nginx serves the built files and forwards `/api` to the backend. Accessible names follow [`../docs/02_contracts/ui-contract.md`](../docs/02_contracts/ui-contract.md).

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 24.13 with npm 11.6
- for the end-to-end tests: the local stack running (see the root README) and Playwright's Chromium (`npx playwright install chromium` once, if it is not installed yet)

## Commands (ES-05)

| Purpose | Command |
|---|---|
| install | `npm ci` |
| build | `npm run build` (type check, then `dist/`) |
| test | `npm test` (unit and acceptance tests) |
| check | `npm run check` (Prettier, ESLint, `tsc --noEmit`) |
| run (development) | `npm run dev`: <http://127.0.0.1:5173/>, `/api` is forwarded to the backend on `127.0.0.1:8080` |
| run (container) | `docker compose --env-file ../.env up -d --build` in `02_output/`: <http://127.0.0.1:8081/> |
| end-to-end tests | `npm run e2e` (needs the running local stack; reads the organizer settings from the repository's `.env`) |
| coverage | `npm run coverage` (report in `coverage/`) |
| mutation score | `npm run mutation` (report in `reports/mutation/`, about 10 minutes) |

## Configuration

The frontend has no secrets (AR-07). Everything it needs comes from the backend's `GET /api/form-config`: the options, the consents, the reCAPTCHA site key and whether test mode is on (then the form sends `test-pass` and shows "reCAPTCHA test mode"). The organizer credentials are typed into the organizer page and kept in memory only.

| Setting | Where | Default |
|---|---|---|
| backend address in development | `vite.config.ts` (`server.proxy`) | `http://127.0.0.1:8080` |
| backend address in the container | `nginx.conf` (`backend:8080`, fixed upstream Host) | compose service `backend` |
| e2e target | `E2E_FRONTEND_URL`, `E2E_BACKEND_URL`, `E2E_MAILPIT_URL` | `http://127.0.0.1:8081`, `:8080`, `:8025` |

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause and fix |
|---|---|
| "The registration form could not be loaded." | the backend is not reachable through `/api`; start it (or the stack) |
| e2e tests time out on the first step | the stack is not running or not healthy: `docker compose --env-file ../.env ps` |
| e2e tests see 429 answers | the API rate limit counts all local browser requests as one client; start the stack with a higher `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` or wait a minute |
| Playwright cannot find a browser | `npx playwright install chromium` |

# Release notes

> Written in: phase 7 · Source: `general/quality/definition-of-done.md`, `docs/06_verification-report.md` · Agent: writes

## Version 1.0.0 (2026-10-22)

First release of the conference registration.

### Features

- Registration for external participants (US-001) and students (US-002) with the fixed fields of BR-01, configurable options grouped as workshops, events, meals and other activities, and the mandatory privacy consent (OQ-02).
- Options and consents from a configuration file, changed by restart without code changes (US-003); every option lists the registration types it is available to (OQ-01).
- Confirmation in the page after the backend accepted the registration, field errors next to the fields, a general message on failure (US-004).
- Storage in PostgreSQL plus a raw JSON copy per registration, both written before success is reported (US-005, AR-05).
- Confirmation email to the participant (US-006) and notification email with the JSON copy attached to every organizer address (US-007); an email failure never undoes a registration (OQ-03).
- Excel export for organizers (US-008) and an organizer search page with text search, type and option filters and paging (US-009), both behind HTTP Basic organizer access.
- Security: reCAPTCHA v2 verified on the server, rate and size limits on every `/api` endpoint, organizer access only over HTTPS except from localhost, security headers, non-root containers.

### Quality

| Component | Tests | Line coverage | Mutation score (adjusted) |
|---|---|---|---|
| backend | 288 (unit, architecture, acceptance) | 98.09 % | 93.15 % |
| frontend | 109 (unit, acceptance) | 100 % | 93.83 % |
| both | 6 end-to-end journeys in Chromium | – | – |

No open Critical, High or Medium finding; accepted items are listed in `docs/06_verification-report.md`.

### Manual tests a human must do (DoD-09)

These cannot be automated without the real external services:

1. **reCAPTCHA with production keys:** with `CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=false` and the real `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`/`RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY`, submit one registration with the widget solved (accepted, 201) and one with an expired or missing token (rejected with a `captchaToken` error, nothing stored).
2. **Email delivery:** with the real SMTP settings, register once and confirm that the participant's real mailbox receives the confirmation and every address in `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` receives the notification with the `registration-<id>.json` attachment; check that Slovenian characters display correctly.
3. **TLS and reverse proxy:** behind the production nginx with Let's Encrypt: HTTPS works and HTTP redirects to HTTPS; `/` serves the frontend and `/api` reaches the backend; the proxy sets the upstream `Host` itself (backend README); with `TRUSTED_PROXIES` set to the proxy's address the organizer page works over HTTPS and an organizer request over plain HTTP is refused.
4. **Organizer page in a real browser:** sign in, search, filter and page through the registrations; no browser login dialog appears on a wrong password.

### Operations

- **Retention (OQ-06):** registrations and JSON copies are kept until the operator deletes them; there is no automatic deletion. Delete the database rows (`registration`, `registration_option`, `registration_consent`) and the files in the JSON copy directory **no later than 12 months after the conference**.
- **Backups:** back up the PostgreSQL volume and the JSON copy volume together.
- **Configuration:** production needs `APP_ENVIRONMENT=production`, `CONFERENCE_CONFIG_FILE`, real reCAPTCHA keys, SMTP settings, `TRUSTED_PROXIES` and `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY=true`; the backend refuses to start otherwise (see the backend README).

### Known limitations and decisions pending review

- D-10: a valid organizer request over plain HTTP from another host is answered 403 (the criteria did not fix a status).
- D-11: the 100-character search limit applies to the text as sent, before surrounding spaces are removed.
- D-08: vitest 4.1.11 has two Moderate advisories (dev tooling only; not in the shipped bundle).
- The organizer page's option filter lists the active options; an inactive option id can still be searched through the API.
- Locally, all browser requests through the frontend container count as one client for the rate limit.

# Conference registration

> Written in: phase 7 · Source: `project/02_design/architecture.md`, ES-06 · Agent: writes

## Overview

Online registration for a conference: external participants and students register through a web form, choose workshops, events, meals and other activities from a configurable list, and give the required consent. Every accepted registration is stored in PostgreSQL and as a raw JSON copy, confirmed to the participant by email and announced to the organizers by email with the JSON copy attached. Organizers search and filter registrations on an organizer page and export them as an Excel workbook.

## Components

| Component | Folder | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| backend | [backend/](backend/README.md) | Spring Boot REST API (`/api`), PostgreSQL via Flyway, JSON copies, emails, reCAPTCHA, organizer access |
| frontend | [frontend/](frontend/README.md) | React single-page app (registration form at `/`, organizer page at `/organizer`) served by nginx, which forwards `/api` to the backend |

The local stack (`docker-compose.yml`) runs both components with PostgreSQL and Mailpit (a local mail catcher).

## Quick start

Prerequisites: Docker Engine with Docker Compose, and a `.env` file at the repository root (one level above this folder):

1. Copy `01_input/01_project/00_setup/secrets.env.example` to `.env` at the repository root and fill in `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `ORGANIZER_USERNAME`, `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` (16+ characters) and `ORGANIZER_EMAILS`. The reCAPTCHA and SMTP keys stay empty locally.
2. Start everything from this folder:

   ```bash
   cd 02_output
   docker compose --env-file ../.env up -d --build
   ```

3. Open:
   - registration form: <http://127.0.0.1:8081/>
   - organizer page: <http://127.0.0.1:8081/organizer> (the organizer credentials from `.env`)
   - emails (Mailpit): <http://127.0.0.1:8025/>
   - API: <http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/form-config>, health <http://127.0.0.1:8080/actuator/health>

4. Stop with `docker compose --env-file ../.env down` (data stays in the named volumes `pgdata` and `jsoncopies`; add `-v` to delete it).

Locally reCAPTCHA runs in test mode (`CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=true`, the form sends the token `test-pass`), organizer access over plain HTTP is allowed (`ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY=false`), and the API allows 60 requests per minute per client and endpoint (`RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE`). All three can be overridden when starting, for example `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE=1000 docker compose --env-file ../.env up -d`.

## Tests

| What | Command | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| backend unit, architecture and acceptance tests | `cd backend && ./mvnw verify` | Docker (Testcontainers) |
| frontend unit and acceptance tests | `cd frontend && npm ci && npm test` | Node |
| end-to-end tests (browser) | `cd frontend && npm run e2e` | the running local stack above |

## Documentation

| Document | Content |
|---|---|
| [docs/02_specification.md](docs/02_specification.md) | architecture, behaviour, settings, traceability |
| [docs/02_contracts/](docs/02_contracts/) | OpenAPI contract, JSON schemas, email and UI contracts |
| [docs/03_test-strategy.md](docs/03_test-strategy.md) | test levels, coverage and mutation results |
| [docs/06_verification-report.md](docs/06_verification-report.md) | verification evidence and findings |
| [docs/release-notes.md](docs/release-notes.md) | release notes and manual tests |
| [docs/decisions-log.md](docs/decisions-log.md) | decisions taken during the build |

# Backend

> Written in: phase 7 · Source: `project/02_design/architecture.md`, ES-05, ES-06 · Agent: writes

Spring Boot REST API of the conference registration (`/api`, contract in [`../docs/02_contracts/openapi.json`](../docs/02_contracts/openapi.json)). Root package `si.konferenca.registration`: `domain` (rules), `application` (use cases and ports), `infrastructure` (database, JSON copies, mail, reCAPTCHA, Excel, configuration), `web` (controllers), `security` (organizer access, HTTPS-only, rate and size limits).

## Prerequisites

- JDK 21 (the Maven wrapper downloads Maven 3.9.9; nothing else to install)
- Docker, for the tests (Testcontainers starts PostgreSQL and Mailpit) and for the container image

## Commands (ES-05)

| Purpose | Command |
|---|---|
| build | `./mvnw -B package -DskipTests` (jar in `target/`) |
| test | `./mvnw -B verify` (all tests; coverage report in `target/site/jacoco/`) |
| check | `./mvnw -B spotless:check compile pmd:check pmd:cpd-check spotbugs:check` |
| run (local stack) | `docker compose --env-file ../.env up -d --build` in `02_output/` |
| run (jar, against your own PostgreSQL and SMTP) | set the settings below as environment variables, then `java -jar target/registration-backend-1.0.0.jar` |
| mutation score | `./mvnw -B test-compile org.pitest:pitest-maven:1.30.0:mutationCoverage` (report in `target/pit-reports/`, about 30 minutes) |
| dependency scan | `NVD_API_KEY=… ./mvnw -B org.owasp:dependency-check-maven:12.1.0:check` |

On Windows use `mvnw.cmd`.

## Configuration

Every environment-specific value is a setting (environment variable); secrets have no default.

| Setting | Default | Source / notes |
|---|---|---|
| `SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL`, `SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME` | `jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/registration`, `registration` | compose sets them |
| `SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD` | none | secret `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` from `.env` |
| `SPRING_MAIL_HOST`, `SPRING_MAIL_PORT` | `localhost`, `1025` | SMTP server; compose uses Mailpit |
| `SPRING_MAIL_USERNAME`, `SPRING_MAIL_PASSWORD`, `SMTP_STARTTLS` | empty, empty, `false` | production SMTP account (secrets `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD`) |
| `MAIL_FROM`, `CONFERENCE_NAME` | `registration@konferenca.si`, `Conference` | sender and conference name in emails |
| `ORGANIZER_USERNAME`, `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` | none | secrets from `.env`; the password is kept only as a BCrypt hash |
| `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` | empty | comma-separated notification recipients |
| `CONFERENCE_CONFIG_FILE` | shipped `conference-config.json` | options and consents (schema [`../docs/02_contracts/conference-config.schema.json`](../docs/02_contracts/conference-config.schema.json)); required in production |
| `JSON_COPY_DIR` | `./data/json-copies` | compose: `/data/json-copies` on the volume `jsoncopies` |
| `CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE` | `false` | `true` accepts only the token `test-pass` (local and test only) |
| `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`, `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` | empty | required unless test mode |
| `RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL` | Google siteverify URL | |
| `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY` | `true` | organizer requests over plain HTTP from other hosts get 403 |
| `TRUSTED_PROXIES` | none | regular expression of proxy IP addresses whose `X-Forwarded-For`/`-Proto` are trusted |
| `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE`, `REQUEST_MAX_BYTES` | `60`, `16384` | per client and endpoint; request body limit |
| `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGIN` | empty | local development only |
| `APP_ENVIRONMENT` | `local` | `production` refuses to start with test mode, plain-HTTP organizer access, CORS or no options file |

Changing the options: edit the configuration file (or point `CONFERENCE_CONFIG_FILE` to another one) and restart; an invalid file stops the start with a message naming the problem.

## Production reverse proxy (SR-08)

The backend container listens on HTTP 8080 behind an nginx that terminates TLS. The proxy sets the upstream `Host` itself and the backend trusts only its address:

```nginx
location /api/ {
    proxy_pass http://backend:8080;
    proxy_set_header Host backend:8080;          # never $host or $http_host
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
}
```

Start the backend with `APP_ENVIRONMENT=production`, `TRUSTED_PROXIES=<nginx IP as regex>`, real reCAPTCHA keys and SMTP settings.

## Health

`/actuator/health`, `/actuator/health/liveness`, `/actuator/health/readiness` (readiness includes the database; a mail outage does not make the backend unready).

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause and fix |
|---|---|
| start fails with "Could not resolve placeholder 'ORGANIZER_USERNAME'" | the organizer secrets are missing; set them (compose reads them from `.env`) |
| start fails with "Refusing to start: …" | the message names the unsafe setting (for example reCAPTCHA keys missing without test mode) |
| start fails with "Invalid conference configuration: …" | fix the named problem in the options file |
| tests fail with "Could not find a valid Docker environment" | start Docker; Testcontainers needs it |
| registrations answer 500 | the JSON copy directory is not writable; check `JSON_COPY_DIR` and the volume |
| 429 answers | over `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` for one client and endpoint; raise it for load tests |

# Frontend

> Written in: phase 7 · Source: `project/02_design/architecture.md`, ES-05, ES-06 · Agent: writes

React single-page app built with Vite: the registration form at `/` and the organizer search page at `/organizer`. It talks to the backend only through `/api` (AR-01); in the container nginx serves the built files and forwards `/api` to the backend. Accessible names follow [`../docs/02_contracts/ui-contract.md`](../docs/02_contracts/ui-contract.md).

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 24.13 with npm 11.6
- for the end-to-end tests: the local stack running (see the root README) and Playwright's Chromium (`npx playwright install chromium` once, if it is not installed yet)

## Commands (ES-05)

| Purpose | Command |
|---|---|
| install | `npm ci` |
| build | `npm run build` (type check, then `dist/`) |
| test | `npm test` (unit and acceptance tests) |
| check | `npm run check` (Prettier, ESLint, `tsc --noEmit`) |
| run (development) | `npm run dev`: <http://127.0.0.1:5173/>, `/api` is forwarded to the backend on `127.0.0.1:8080` |
| run (container) | `docker compose --env-file ../.env up -d --build` in `02_output/`: <http://127.0.0.1:8081/> |
| end-to-end tests | `npm run e2e` (needs the running local stack; reads the organizer settings from the repository's `.env`) |
| coverage | `npm run coverage` (report in `coverage/`) |
| mutation score | `npm run mutation` (report in `reports/mutation/`, about 10 minutes) |

## Configuration

The frontend has no secrets (AR-07). Everything it needs comes from the backend's `GET /api/form-config`: the options, the consents, the reCAPTCHA site key and whether test mode is on (then the form sends `test-pass` and shows "reCAPTCHA test mode"). The organizer credentials are typed into the organizer page and kept in memory only.

| Setting | Where | Default |
|---|---|---|
| backend address in development | `vite.config.ts` (`server.proxy`) | `http://127.0.0.1:8080` |
| backend address in the container | `nginx.conf` (`backend:8080`, fixed upstream Host) | compose service `backend` |
| e2e target | `E2E_FRONTEND_URL`, `E2E_BACKEND_URL`, `E2E_MAILPIT_URL` | `http://127.0.0.1:8081`, `:8080`, `:8025` |

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause and fix |
|---|---|
| "The registration form could not be loaded." | the backend is not reachable through `/api`; start it (or the stack) |
| e2e tests time out on the first step | the stack is not running or not healthy: `docker compose --env-file ../.env ps` |
| e2e tests see 429 answers | the API rate limit counts all local browser requests as one client; start the stack with a higher `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` or wait a minute |
| Playwright cannot find a browser | `npx playwright install chromium` |

# Release notes

> Written in: phase 7 · Source: `general/quality/definition-of-done.md`, `docs/06_verification-report.md` · Agent: writes

## Version 1.0.0 (2026-10-22)

First release of the conference registration.

### Features

- Registration for external participants (US-001) and students (US-002) with the fixed fields of BR-01, configurable options grouped as workshops, events, meals and other activities, and the mandatory privacy consent (OQ-02).
- Options and consents from a configuration file, changed by restart without code changes (US-003); every option lists the registration types it is available to (OQ-01).
- Confirmation in the page after the backend accepted the registration, field errors next to the fields, a general message on failure (US-004).
- Storage in PostgreSQL plus a raw JSON copy per registration, both written before success is reported (US-005, AR-05).
- Confirmation email to the participant (US-006) and notification email with the JSON copy attached to every organizer address (US-007); an email failure never undoes a registration (OQ-03).
- Excel export for organizers (US-008) and an organizer search page with text search, type and option filters and paging (US-009), both behind HTTP Basic organizer access.
- Security: reCAPTCHA v2 verified on the server, rate and size limits on every `/api` endpoint, organizer access only over HTTPS except from localhost, security headers, non-root containers.

### Quality

| Component | Tests | Line coverage | Mutation score (adjusted) |
|---|---|---|---|
| backend | 288 (unit, architecture, acceptance) | 98.09 % | 93.15 % |
| frontend | 109 (unit, acceptance) | 100 % | 93.83 % |
| both | 6 end-to-end journeys in Chromium | – | – |

No open Critical, High or Medium finding; accepted items are listed in `docs/06_verification-report.md`.

### Manual tests a human must do (DoD-09)

These cannot be automated without the real external services:

1. **reCAPTCHA with production keys:** with `CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=false` and the real `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`/`RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY`, submit one registration with the widget solved (accepted, 201) and one with an expired or missing token (rejected with a `captchaToken` error, nothing stored).
2. **Email delivery:** with the real SMTP settings, register once and confirm that the participant's real mailbox receives the confirmation and every address in `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` receives the notification with the `registration-<id>.json` attachment; check that Slovenian characters display correctly.
3. **TLS and reverse proxy:** behind the production nginx with Let's Encrypt: HTTPS works and HTTP redirects to HTTPS; `/` serves the frontend and `/api` reaches the backend; the proxy sets the upstream `Host` itself (backend README); with `TRUSTED_PROXIES` set to the proxy's address the organizer page works over HTTPS and an organizer request over plain HTTP is refused.
4. **Organizer page in a real browser:** sign in, search, filter and page through the registrations; no browser login dialog appears on a wrong password.

### Operations

- **Retention (OQ-06):** registrations and JSON copies are kept until the operator deletes them; there is no automatic deletion. Delete the database rows (`registration`, `registration_option`, `registration_consent`) and the files in the JSON copy directory **no later than 12 months after the conference**.
- **Backups:** back up the PostgreSQL volume and the JSON copy volume together.
- **Configuration:** production needs `APP_ENVIRONMENT=production`, `CONFERENCE_CONFIG_FILE`, real reCAPTCHA keys, SMTP settings, `TRUSTED_PROXIES` and `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY=true`; the backend refuses to start otherwise (see the backend README).

### Known limitations and decisions pending review

- D-10: a valid organizer request over plain HTTP from another host is answered 403 (the criteria did not fix a status).
- D-11: the 100-character search limit applies to the text as sent, before surrounding spaces are removed.
- D-08: vitest 4.1.11 has two Moderate advisories (dev tooling only; not in the shipped bundle).
- The organizer page's option filter lists the active options; an inactive option id can still be searched through the API.
- Locally, all browser requests through the frontend container count as one client for the rate limit.

6	
7	## Prerequisites
8	
9	- Node.js 24.13 with npm 11.6
10	- for the end-to-end tests: the local stack running (see the root README) and Playwright's Chromium (`npx playwright install chromium` once, if it is not installed yet)
11	
12	## Commands (ES-05)
13	
14	| Purpose           | Command                                                                                                  |
15	| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
16	| install           | `npm ci`                                                                                                 |
17	| build             | `npm run build` (type check, then `dist/`)                                                               |
18	| test              | `npm test` (unit and acceptance tests)                                                                   |
19	| check             | `npm run check` (Prettier, ESLint, `tsc --noEmit`)                                                       |
20	| run (development) | `npm run dev`: <http://127.0.0.1:5173/>, `/api` is forwarded to the backend on `127.0.0.1:8080`          |
21	| run (container)   | `docker compose --env-file ../.env up -d --build` in `02_output/`: <http://127.0.0.1:8081/>              |
22	| end-to-end tests  | `npm run e2e` (needs the running local stack; reads the organizer settings from the repository's `.env`) |
23	| coverage          | `npm run coverage` (report in `coverage/`)                                                               |
24	| mutation score    | `npm run mutation` (report in `reports/mutation/`, about 10 minutes)                                     |
25	
26	## Configuration
27	
28	The frontend has no secrets (AR-07). Everything it needs comes from the backend's `GET /api/form-config`: the options, the consents, the reCAPTCHA site key and whether test mode is on (then the form sends `test-pass` and shows "reCAPTCHA test mode"). The organizer credentials are typed into the organizer page and kept in memory only.
29	
30	| Setting                          | Where                                                    | Default                                   |
31	| -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
32	| backend address in development   | `vite.config.ts` (`server.proxy`)                        | `http://127.0.0.1:8080`                   |
33	| backend address in the container | `nginx.conf` (`backend:8080`, fixed upstream Host)       | compose service `backend`                 |
34	| e2e target                       | `E2E_FRONTEND_URL`, `E2E_BACKEND_URL`, `E2E_MAILPIT_URL` | `http://127.0.0.1:8081`, `:8080`, `:8025` |
35	
36	## Troubleshooting
37	
38	| Symptom                                      | Cause and fix                                                                                                                              |
39	| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
40	| "The registration form could not be loaded." | the backend is not reachable through `/api`; start it (or the stack)                                                                       |
41	| e2e tests time out on the first step         | the stack is not running or not healthy: `docker compose --env-file ../.env ps`                                                            |
42	| e2e tests see 429 answers                    | the API rate limit counts all local browser requests as one client; start the stack with a higher `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` or wait a minute |
43	| Playwright cannot find a browser             | `npx playwright install chromium`                                                                                                          |

All seven phases are finished and every gate passed. The run ended at commit `2043b38`. The post-run report hook should now build `03_statistics/results/`. I left `run-summary.md` and `run-log.json` uncommitted, as the Run Guide expects; you commit and push them afterwards.

**What was delivered:**
- **Backend:** a Spring Boot API with registration, configurable options, PostgreSQL storage plus a raw JSON copy, confirmation and organizer emails, Excel export and search. Organizer access is protected and requests are rate- and size-limited.
- **Frontend:** a React registration form and an organizer search page, served by nginx. The whole stack starts locally with `docker compose --env-file ../.env up -d --build` in `02_output/`.
- **Tests:** all 48 acceptance criteria are covered by frozen tests and none of them was changed. The final run had 403 tests and none failed, including the 6 end-to-end browser journeys.

| | Line coverage | Mutation score | Survivor rounds |
|---|---|---|---|
| Backend | 98.09% | 93.15% | 0 |
| Frontend | 100% | 93.83% | 1 |

Both parts meet the gate of 95% line coverage and 90% mutation score.

- **Verification:** both hash manifests still match and no secret leaked into files or commit messages. There is no open Critical or High finding. The one finding worth fixing, a Medium Semgrep warning in a contract-checking script (F-01), is fixed. The other seven are accepted with reasons in `docs/06_verification-report.md`.
- **Runtime:** registrations, emails, export and search all worked against the running stack, and the data survived recreating every container. The READMEs work from a clean clone.

**Problems I fixed along the way:**
- The first clean-clone attempt failed on Windows path length. I redid it with long paths enabled.
- That run showed `npm run check` failing because the frontend README I had just written wasn't formatted. I fixed it in `bfbcf85`, and the second clean-clone pass is green.

**Rule breaches recorded in the run log:** five commits went over the 400-line limit. Two are build commits (Maven wrapper scripts and the npm lock file), two are test-harness commits, and one is a unit-test commit at 408 lines. The phase 3 tests were also committed in quick succession, so they'll show up as bursts.

**For you:**
- Run the four manual tests listed in `docs/release-notes.md`: real reCAPTCHA keys, real mail delivery, the production nginx with TLS, and the organizer page in a real browser.
- Review the three decisions I made and marked as pending review:
  - **D-10:** a plain-HTTP organizer request from another host gets 403.
  - **D-11:** the 100-character search limit counts surrounding spaces.
  - **D-08:** vitest 4.1.11 has two moderate advisories, in dev tooling only.
